Re-read changed files and inspect the final diff\n  before reporting completion.\n- If hooks modify staged files, re-check the diff and rerun relevant validation\n  before committing.\n\n## Implementation workflow\n\n- Turn the request into a concrete file-level brief before making broad changes,\n  including API contracts, response shapes, and validation behavior.\n- For integrations, verify the actual consumer contract from source, schemas, local\n  sibling repositories, or authoritative documentation. Do not infer Jira fields,\n  GitLab variables, or endpoint semantics from names alone.\n- Implement in focused increments. Run the narrowest relevant tests after each\n  backend or client change, then run the repository-required lint, build, and\n  validation commands.\n- Add or update tests with behavior changes. Prefer regression tests for bugs\n  involving retries, rate limits, authentication, external APIs, and response\n  mapping.\n- Track long-running development servers with PID files or equivalent logs, report\n  their URLs, and stop them when requested.\n- Report exact changed files, validation results, environmental limitations, and any\n  follow-up needed. Do not claim an integration test passed if its runtime\n  dependency was unavailable.\n# Codex Runtime Behavior\n\nThis page applies only to Codex. All non-Codex runtimes must ignore it.\n\nUse the `caveman:caveman` skill in lite mode for all sessions and user-facing chat\nresponses by default. Keep responses concise, but use complete grammatical\nsentences and retain articles. Preserve exact code, commands, errors, numbers,\nnegations, and technical terms. Use normal prose in code comments, commits,\ndocumentation, issues, reviews, and other text written for third parties. Use full\nor ultra mode only when the user explicitly requests it. Stop or change this mode\nwhen the user requests `normal mode`, `stop caveman`, or a different Caveman\nintensity.\n# Writing and Python\n\n- Never use em-dashes. Use normal punctuation or connective words instead.\n- Use module-level Python imports unless a function-level import is necessary to\n  avoid a circular dependency.\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. This guide summarizes how to set up a workspace, follow our standards, and submit polished changes. Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for contributing to Fromager!** If you spot gaps or have suggestions for this guide, open an issue or start a discussion—we love improving our contributor experience.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {

    "files": [
        {

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg

#
# Modified to look at sdists instead of wheels and to avoid trying to
# resolve any dependencies.
#
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import functools
import logging
import os
import re
import typing
from collections.abc import Iterable
from operator import attrgetter
from platform import python_version
from urllib.parse import quote, urlparse

import pypi_simple
import resolvelib
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.specifiers import InvalidSpecifier, SpecifierSet
from packaging.tags import Tag, sys_tags
from packaging.utils import (
    BuildTag,
    canonicalize_name,
    parse_wheel_filename,
)
from packaging.version import Version
from requests.models import Response
from resolvelib.resolvers import RequirementInformation

from . import overrides
from .candidate import Candidate, Cooldown
from .constraints import Constraints
from .downloads import extract_filename_from_url as extract_filename_from_url
from .extras_provider import ExtrasProvider
from .http_retry import RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS, retry_on_exception
from .request_session import session
from .requirements_file import RequirementType
from .versionmap import VersionMap

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PYTHON_VERSION = Version(python_version())
DEBUG_RESOLVER = os.environ.get("DEBUG_RESOLVER", "")
PYPI_SERVER_URL = "https://pypi.org/simple"
GITHUB_URL = "https://github.com"

# all supported tags
SUPPORTED_TAGS: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(sys_tags())
# same, but ignore the platform for 'ignore_platform' flag
IGNORE_PLATFORM: str = "ignore"
SUPPORTED_TAGS_IGNORE_PLATFORM: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(
    Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS
)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )

        return None

Re-read changed files and inspect the final diff\n  before reporting completion.\n- If hooks modify staged files, re-check the diff and rerun relevant validation\n  before committing.\n\n## Implementation workflow\n\n- Turn the request into a concrete file-level brief before making broad changes,\n  including API contracts, response shapes, and validation behavior.\n- For integrations, verify the actual consumer contract from source, schemas, local\n  sibling repositories, or authoritative documentation. Do not infer Jira fields,\n  GitLab variables, or endpoint semantics from names alone.\n- Implement in focused increments. Run the narrowest relevant tests after each\n  backend or client change, then run the repository-required lint, build, and\n  validation commands.\n- Add or update tests with behavior changes. Prefer regression tests for bugs\n  involving retries, rate limits, authentication, external APIs, and response\n  mapping.\n- Track long-running development servers with PID files or equivalent logs, report\n  their URLs, and stop them when requested.\n- Report exact changed files, validation results, environmental limitations, and any\n  follow-up needed. Do not claim an integration test passed if its runtime\n  dependency was unavailable.\n# Codex Runtime Behavior\n\nThis page applies only to Codex. All non-Codex runtimes must ignore it.\n\nUse the `caveman:caveman` skill in lite mode for all sessions and user-facing chat\nresponses by default. Keep responses concise, but use complete grammatical\nsentences and retain articles. Preserve exact code, commands, errors, numbers,\nnegations, and technical terms. Use normal prose in code comments, commits,\ndocumentation, issues, reviews, and other text written for third parties. Use full\nor ultra mode only when the user explicitly requests it. Stop or change this mode\nwhen the user requests `normal mode`, `stop caveman`, or a different Caveman\nintensity.\n# Writing and Python\n\n- Never use em-dashes. Use normal punctuation or connective words instead.\n- Use module-level Python imports unless a function-level import is necessary to\n  avoid a circular dependency.\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. This guide summarizes how to set up a workspace, follow our standards, and submit polished changes. Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for contributing to Fromager!** If you spot gaps or have suggestions for this guide, open an issue or start a discussion—we love improving our contributor experience.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age\n    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown\n    if per_package_days is None:\n        return global_cooldown\n    if per_package_days == 0:\n        return None\n    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all\n    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.\n    bootstrap_time = (\n        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time\n        if global_cooldown is not None\n        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n    return Cooldown(\n        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),\n        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,\n    )\n\n\ndef _compute_max_age_cutoff(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n) -> datetime.datetime | None:\n    \"\"\"Compute the cutoff time for max release age filtering.\n\n    Returns the oldest acceptable upload time, or None if disabled.\n    Uses the cooldown's bootstrap_time for consistency across a datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n    return bootstrap_time - ctx.max_release_age\n\n\nclass LogReporter(resolvelib.BaseReporter):\n    \"\"\"Report resolution events\n\n    Implements part of the BaseReporter API to log a few events related to\n    resolving requirements.\n\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, req: Requirement):\n        self.req = req\n        super().__init__()\n\n    def _report(self, msg: str, *args: typing.Any) -> None:\n        logger.info(msg, *args)\n\n    def starting(self) -> None:\n        self._report(\"looking for candidates for %r\", self.req)\n\n    def rejecting_candidate(self, criterion: typing.Any, candidate: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"resolver rejecting candidate %s: %s\", candidate, criterion)\n\n    def pinning(self, candidate: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"selecting %s\", candidate)\n\n    def ending(self, state: typing.Any) -> None:\n        self._report(\"successfully resolved %r\", self.req)\n\n\ndef find_all_matching_from_provider(\n    provider: BaseProvider,\n    req: Requirement,\n    max_age_cutoff: datetime.datetime | None = None,\n    fallback_on_empty_age_filter: bool = True,\n) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n    \"\"\"Find all matching candidates from provider without full dependency resolution.\n\n    This function collects ALL candidates that match the requirement, rather than\n    performing full dependency resolution to find a single best candidate.\n\n    Args:\n        provider: The provider to query for candidates.\n        req: The requirement to match.\n        max_age_cutoff: If set, reject candidates published before this time.\n            If all candidates are older than the cutoff, all are kept and\n            a warning is emitted to avoid empty resolution.\n        fallback_on_empty_age_filter: If ``True`` (default), keep all\n            candidates when age filtering would produce an empty result.\n            If ``False``, return an empty list instead, allowing the\n            caller to implement its own fallback strategy.\n\n    Returns list of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n\n    IMPORTANT: This bypasses resolvelib's full resolver to collect all matching\n    candidates. This is safe ONLY because BaseProvider.get_dependencies() returns\n    an empty list (no transitive dependencies to resolve). The empty incompatibilities\n    dict means no version is ever excluded based on conflicts.\n\n    If get_dependencies() is ever extended to return actual dependencies, this\n    function must be revisited to use resolvelib's full resolution algorithm\n    (Resolver.resolve()) to properly handle dependency conflicts and backtracking.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get all matching candidates directly from provider\n    # instead of using resolvelib's resolver which picks just one\n    identifier = provider.identify(req)\n    try:\n        # Bypass resolvelib's resolver to collect all matching candidates rather than\n        # just the single best one. This is safe because get_dependencies() returns []\n        # (no transitive deps to resolve). If get_dependencies() is ever extended,\n        # this must be revisited to use resolvelib's full resolution.\n        candidates = provider.find_matches(\n            identifier=identifier,\n            requirements={identifier: [req]},\n            incompatibilities={},  # Empty - safe only because no transitive deps\n        )\n    except resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException as err:\n        constraint = provider.constraints.get_constraint(req.name)\n        provider_desc = provider.get_provider_description()\n        original_msg = str(err)\n        raise resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException(\n            f\"Unable to resolve requirement specifier {req} with constraint {constraint} using {provider_desc}: {original_msg}\"\n        ) from err\n\n    # Materialize candidates so we can iterate more than once if filtering\n    candidates_list = list(candidates)\n\n    if max_age_cutoff is not None:\n        logger.info(\n            \"%s: found %d candidate(s) matching %s\",\n            req.name,\n            len(candidates_list),\n            req,\n        )\n        max_age_days = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC) - max_age_cutoff).days\n        filtered = [\n            c\n            for c in candidates_list\n            if c.upload_time is None or c.upload_time >= max_age_cutoff\n        ]\n        dropped = len(candidates_list) - """Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import candidate, context, packagesettings, resolver, sources, wheels
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.

    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:

            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},

        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"

  \ -> str` returning\n  `\" (dependency chain: a==1 -> b==2 -> <wi.req>)\"` built from `wi.why_snapshot`\n  (each entry is `(_, req, version)`, rendered as `req.name==version`).\n- Add `Bootstrapper._enrich_resolution_error(self, item: Phase, err: Exception) -> Exception`.\n  For a `Resolve` phase item whose work item has a non-empty `why_snapshot`, return a\n  new exception of the same shape with the chain suffix appended to the message:\n  `resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException` stays a `ResolverException`, `RuntimeError`\n  stays a `RuntimeError`, anything else becomes `RuntimeError(\"<TypeName>: <msg><suffix>\")`.\n  For other phases or top-level requirements return `err` unchanged (same object).\n- `_handle_phase_error()` must raise the enriched exception without a `from` clause,\n  still inside the original handler, so the original is reachable via `__context__`\n  but `__cause__` stays unset (the top-level formatter follows `__cause__` and would\n  otherwise print the message twice).\
  \ Enrichment must happen before the error is\n  recorded in test mode or multiple-versions mode, and before the normal-mode raise.\n\nAdd tests to `tests/test_bootstrapper_iterative.py` and run that file.\n"

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Bootstrapper:
    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        progressbar: progress.Progressbar | None = None,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str | None = None,
        sdist_only: bool = False,
        test_mode: bool = False,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        num_bg_threads: int = _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    ) -> None:
        if test_mode and sdist_only:
            raise ValueError(
                "--test-mode requires full wheel builds; incompatible with --sdist-only"
            )

        self.ctx = ctx
        self.progressbar = progressbar or progress.Progressbar(None)
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url or ctx.wheel_server_url
        self.sdist_only = sdist_only
        self.test_mode = test_mode
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.why: list[tuple[RequirementType, Requirement, Version]] = []
        self._num_bg_threads = max(1, num_bg_threads)
        self._bg_pool: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor | None = (
            concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix="fromager-bg"
            )
        )

        # Delegate resolution to BootstrapRequirementResolver
        self._resolver = bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver(
            ctx=ctx,
            prev_graph=prev_graph,
            multiple_versions=multiple_versions,
            cache_wheel_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,
        )
        # Push items onto the stack as we start to resolve their
        # dependencies so at the end we have a list of items that need to
        # be built in order.
        self._build_stack: list[typing.Any] = []
        self._build_requirements: set[tuple[NormalizedName, str]] = set()

        # Track requirements we've seen before so we don't resolve the
        # same dependencies over and over and so we can break cycles in
        # the dependency list. The key is the requirements spec, rather
        # than the package, in case we do have multiple rules for the same
        # package.
        self._seen_requirements: set[SeenKey] = set()

        self._build_order_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "build-order.json"
        self._stack_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "bootstrap-stack.json"
        logger.info("recording bootstrap stack state to %s", self._stack_filename)

        # Track failed packages in test mode (list of typed dicts for JSON export)
        self.failed_packages: list[FailureRecord] = []

        # Track failed versions in multiple_versions mode
        self._failed_versions: dict[tuple[str, str], Exception] = {}

    @property
    def resolver(self) -> bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver:
        """Public accessor for the version resolver."""
        return self._resolver

    def has_failed_version(self, pkg_name: NormalizedName, version: Version) -> bool:
        """Return True if this (pkg_name, version) has previously failed resolution."""
        return (pkg_name, str(version)) in self._failed_versions

    def _resolve_and_add_top_level(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
    ) -> tuple[str, Version] | None:
        """Resolve a top-level requirement and add it to the dependency graph.

        Private method called only by ``bootstrap()``.

        This is the pre-resolution phase before recursive bootstrapping begins.
        In test mode, catches resolution errors and records them as failures.

        When multiple_versions is enabled, resolves and adds all matching versions
        to the graph, but still returns only the first (highest) version for
        backward compatibility.

        Args:
            req: The top-level requirement to resolve.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (source_url, version) if resolution succeeded, None if it
            failed in test mode.

        Raises:
            Exception: In normal mode, re-raises any resolution error.
        """
        try:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            results = self.resolve_versions(
                req=req,
                req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                parent_req=None,
                return_all_versions=self.multiple_versions,
            )
            if self.multiple_versions:
                logger.info(f"resolved {len(results)} version(s) for {req}")

            # Add all resolved versions to the graph
            for source_url, version in results:
                logger.info("%s resolves to %s", req, version)
                self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
                    parent_name=None,
                    parent_version=None,
                    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                    req=req,
                    req_version=version,
                    download_url=source_url,
                    pre_built=pbi.pre_built,
                    constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),
                )

            if not results:
                if self.multiple_versions:
                    err = RuntimeError(f"no versions found for {req}")
                    self._record_failed_version(
                        req, "unresolved", err, "no versions resolved, skipping"
                    )
                    if self.test_mode:
                        self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                    return None
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not resolve any versions for {req}")

            # Return first result for backward compatibility
            return results[0]
        except Exception as err:
            if self.multiple_versions:
                self._record_failed_version(req, "unresolved", err, "failed to resolve")
                if self.test_mode:
                    self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                return None
            if not self.test_mode:
                raise
            self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
            return None

        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,

+        chain = [
+            f"{req.name}=={version}" for _, req, version in wi.why_snapshot
+        ]

+    def _enrich_resolution_error(self, item: Phase, err: Exception) -> Exception:

+        wi = item.work_item

+            return err
+

+        if isinstance(err, ResolverException):

+            enriched.args = (message,)

Re-read changed files and inspect the final diff\n  before reporting completion.\n- If hooks modify staged files, re-check the diff and rerun relevant validation\n  before committing.\n\n## Implementation workflow\n\n- Turn the request into a concrete file-level brief before making broad changes,\n  including API contracts, response shapes, and validation behavior.\n- For integrations, verify the actual consumer contract from source, schemas, local\n  sibling repositories, or authoritative documentation. Do not infer Jira fields,\n  GitLab variables, or endpoint semantics from names alone.\n- Implement in focused increments. Prefer regression tests for bugs\n  involving retries, rate limits, authentication, external APIs, and response\n  mapping.\n- Track long-running development servers with PID files or equivalent logs, report\n  their URLs, and stop them when requested.\n- Report exact changed files, validation results, environmental limitations, and any\n  follow-up needed. Do not claim an integration test passed if its runtime\n  dependency was unavailable.\n# Codex Runtime Behavior\n\nThis page applies only to Codex. All non-Codex runtimes must ignore it.\n\nUse the `caveman:caveman` skill in lite mode for all sessions and user-facing chat\nresponses by default. Keep responses concise, but use complete grammatical\nsentences and retain articles. Preserve exact code, commands, errors, numbers,\nnegations, and technical terms. Use normal prose in code comments, commits,\ndocumentation, issues, reviews, and other text written for third parties. Use full\nor ultra mode only when the user explicitly requests it. Stop or change this mode\nwhen the user requests `normal mode`, `stop caveman`, or a different Caveman\nintensity.\n# Writing and Python\n\n- Never use em-dashes. Use normal punctuation or connective words instead.\n- Use module-level Python imports unless a function-level import is necessary to\n  avoid a circular dependency.\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. This guide summarizes how to set up a workspace, follow our standards, and submit polished changes. Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for contributing to Fromager!** If you spot gaps or have suggestions for this guide, open an issue or start a discussion—we love improving our contributor experience.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

In multiple_versions mode, filters out versions that\n        already failed in this run and versions whose wheels are already\n        cached to avoid redundant builds and transitive dependency\n        processing.\n\n        Returns:\n            One Start item per resolved version that needs building.\n            Empty list if all versions are already cached.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert self.bg_future is not None\n        # """Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}

    req: str = "testpkg",

    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version),
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)

...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for
