In all other\n                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.\n            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.\n                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.ctx = ctx\n        self.prev_graph = prev_graph\n        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions\n        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url\n        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution\n        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types\n        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.\n        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)\n        # Value: {version: url}\n        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}\n        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.\n        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)\n        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.\n        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()\n        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def resolve(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,\n        pre_built: bool | None = None,\n        return_all_versions: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).\n\n        Uses a two-step strategy:\n        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch\n           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the\n           package-level known-versions cache.\n        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current\n           requirement specifier.\n\n        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,\n        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups\n        with different specifiers for the same package.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain\n            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).\n                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.\n            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,\n                return only the highest matching version.\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching\n            versions when return_all_versions=True.\n\n        Raises:\n            ValueError: If req contains a git URL and pre_built is False\n None:\n            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n            pre_built = pbi.pre_built\n\n        # Check session cache BEFORE the git URL guard so that background\n        # threads can retrieve pre-cached git URL resolutions (populated by\n        # Bootstrapper.resolve_versions() on the main thread before bootstrap()\n        # is called) without hitting the ValueError.\n        cached_result = self.get_cached_resolution(req, pre_built)\n        if cached_result is not None:\n            logger.debug(f\"resolved {req} from cache\")\n            return list(cached_result) if or network and\n                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.\n                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)\n self.cache_wheel_server_url:\n                logger.info(\n                    \"no results found with normal resolution, \"\n                    \"falling back to the cache server %s\",\n     \"resolver returned no results \"\n                    \"(wheel server URL %s, %s version mode)\",\n                    self.cache_wheel_server_url or \"(none)\",\n                    \"multiple\" if self.multiple_versions else \"single\",\n                )\n\n        if results:\n            self._extend_known_versions(req, pre_built, results)\n\n    def _resolve_from_cache_server(self, req: Requirement) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Fall back to the remote wheel cache server for a cached version.\n\n        When age filtering removes all candidates in multi-version mode,\n version.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(\n            \"checking cache server %s for existing build\",\n            self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n        )\n        best: tuple[str, Version] | None = None\n        for include_sdists, include_wheels in [(False, True), (True, False)]:\n            try:\n                provider = finders.PyPICacheProvider(\n                    cache_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n                    constraints=self.ctx.constraints,\n                    include_sdists=include_sdists,\n                    include_wheels=include_wheels,\n                )\n                results = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(provider, req)\n                if results:\n                    url, version = results[0]\n                    if best is None or version > best[1]:\n                        best = (url, version)\n            except Exception as err:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"error checking cache server %s: %s\",\n                    self.cache_wheel_server_url,\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport typing\n\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.utils import canonicalize_name\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom .. import bootstrap_requirement_resolver\nfrom ..log import req_ctxvar_context\nfrom ..requirements_file import RequirementType\nfrom . import _cache\nfrom ._phase import Phase\nfrom ._start import Start\nfrom ._types import BootstrapPhase\nfrom ._work_item import WorkItem\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from ._bootstrapper import Bootstrapper\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef _bg_resolve(\n    bg_resolver: bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver,\n    req: Requirement,\n    req_type: RequirementType,\n    parent_req: Requirement | None,\n    return_all_versions: bool,\n) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n    \"\"\"Background-safe resolution: no Bootstrapper state accessed.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(f\"{BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE} for {req_type} requirement\")\n    return bg_resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=req_type,\n        parent_req=parent_req,\n        return_all_versions=return_all_versions,\n    )\n\n\nclass Resolve(Phase):\n    \"\"\"Resolve a requirement's available version(s) and fan out to ``Start`` items.\n\n    Resolution runs in a background thread (via ``background_work``); ``run()``\n    blocks until the result is ready.  In normal mode the highest matching\n    version is used; in ``multiple_versions`` mode every candidate version is\n    returned, minus any that previously failed or whose wheels are already\n    cached.\n\n    Next phase: one ``Start`` item per version that still needs processing.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    phase: typing.ClassVar[BootstrapPhase] = BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE\n    tracks_why: typing.ClassVar[bool] = False\n\n    def background_work(\n        self, bt: Bootstrapper\n    ) -> typing.Callable[[], typing.Any] | None:\n        \"\"\"Return closure that calls ``_bg_resolve`` in a thread.\"\"\"\n        bg_resolver = bt.resolver\n        req = self.work_item.req\n        req_type = self.work_item.req_type\n        parent_req = (\n            self.work_item.why_snapshot[-1][1] if self.work_item.why_snapshot else None\n        )\n        return_all = bt.multiple_versions\n\n        def do_resolve() -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n            with req_ctxvar_context(req):\n                return _bg_resolve(bg_resolver, req, req_type, parent_req, return_all)\n\n        return do_resolve\n\n    def run(self, bt: Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"RESOLVE phase: resolve versions and expand into Start items.\n\n        Centralizes version resolution so all dependencies are expanded\n        uniformly. In multiple_versions mode, filters out versions that\n        already failed in this run and versions whose wheels are already\n        cached to avoid redundant builds and transitive dependency\n        processing.\n\n        Returns:\n            One Start item per resolved version that needs building.\n            Empty list if all versions are already cached.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert self.bg_future is not None\n        # bg_future.result() blocks until the background resolution completes,\n        # then returns the result or re-raises any exception from the background.\n        resolved_versions = self.bg_future.result()\n        if not resolved_versions:\n            raise RuntimeError(\n                f\"Could not resolve any versions for {self.work_item.req}\"\n            )\n\n        if bt.multiple_versions:\n            pkg_name = canonicalize_name(self.work_item.req.name)\n            resolved_versions = [\n                (url, ver)\n                for url, ver in resolved_versions\n                if not bt.has_failed_version(pkg_name, ver)\n            ]\n            if not resolved_versions:\n                raise RuntimeError(\n                    f\"Could not resolve any versions for {self.work_item.req}\"\n                    f\" (all candidates failed previously)\"\n                )\n\n            logger.info(\n                f\"resolved {len(resolved_versions)} version(s) for {self.work_item.req}\"\n            )\n            filtered: list[tuple[str, Version]] = []\n            for source_url, version in resolved_versions:\n                cached_wheel, _ = _cache._find_cached_wheel(\n                    bt.ctx, bt.cache_wheel_server_url, self.work_item.req, version\n                )\n                if cached_wheel:\n                    logger.info(\n                        f\"{self.work_item.req.name}=={version}: wheel already cached \"\n                        f\"at {cached_wheel.name}, skipping\"\n                    )\n                else:\n                    filtered.append((source_url, version))\n            if not filtered:\n                # Always process the highest version (first in\n                # resolved_versions) so new transitive dependencies\n                # are discovered even when every wheel is cached.\n                logger.info(\n                    f\"all versions of {self.work_item.req.name} already cached, \"\n                    f\"keeping highest version {resolved_versions[0][1]} \"\n                    f\"for dependency discovery\"\n                )\n                filtered.append(resolved_versions[0])\n            resolved_versions = filtered\n\n        # Build list so highest version ends up on top of the stack\n        # (last element after extend) and is processed first.\n        items: list[Phase] = []\n        for source_url, version in reversed(resolved_versions):\n            items.append(\n                Start(\n                    WorkItem(\n                        req=self.work_item.req,\n                        req_type=self.work_item.req_type,\n                        why_snapshot=list(self.work_item.why_snapshot),\n                        parent=self.work_item.parent,\n                        source_url=source_url,\n                        resolved_version=version,\n                    )\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Contains one item when\n            return_all_versions=False, or all matching versions when True.\n        \"\"\"\n        if req.url:\n            if req_type != RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL:\n                raise ValueError(\n                    f\"{req} includes a URL, but is not a top-level dependency\"\n                )\n\n            # Check cache first to avoid re-resolving\n            # Git URLs are always source (not prebuilt)\n            cached_result = self._resolver.get_matching_versions(req, pre_built=False)\n            if cached_result:\n                logger.debug(f\"resolved {req} from cache\")\n                return cached_result if return_all_versions else [cached_result[0]]\n\n            logger.info(\"resolving source via URL, ignoring any plugins\")\n            source_url, resolved_version = self._resolve_version_from_git_url(req=req)\n            # Cache the git URL resolution (always source, not prebuilt)\n            # Store as list for consistency with cache structure\n            result = [(source_url, resolved_version)]\n            self._resolver.extend_known_versions(req, pre_built=False, result=result)\n            return result  # Git URLs always return single version\n\n        # Delegate to RequirementResolver\n        return self._resolver.resolve(\n            req=req,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            parent_req=parent_req,\n            return_all_versions=return_all_versions,\n        )\n\n    def bootstrap(self, requirements: list[Requirement]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap all top-level requirements and their transitive dependencies.\n\n        .. versionadded:: 0.89\n           Replaces the former ``bootstrap(req, req_type)`` signature.\n\n        Resolves each requirement, adds it to the dependency graph, and processes\n        the full dependency tree using an iterative DFS loop. Handles\n        ``requirement_ctxvar`` context internally; callers do not need to manage it.\n\n        In test mode, records failures and continues instead of raising. In\n        ``multiple_versions`` mode, processes all matching versions per requirement.\n\n        Args:\n            requirements: Top-level requirements to resolve and bootstrap.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Resolve all top-level reqs and build initial stack.\n        # Use the token pattern (no try/finally) so that if resolution raises\n        # in normal mode, the context var stays set for the top-level error\n        # handler in __main__.py to include the package name in its log message.\n        stack: list[Phase] = []\n        initial_items: list[Phase] = []\n        for req in requirements:\n            token = requirement_ctxvar.set(req)\n            result = self._resolve_and_add_top_level(req)\n            requirement_ctxvar.reset(token)\n            if result is not None:\n                initial_items.append(\n                    Resolve(\n                        WorkItem(\n                            req=req,\n                            req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n                            why_snapshot=[],\n                            parent=None,\n                        )\n                    )\n                )\n        self._push_items(stack, initial_items)\n\n        self._run_bootstrap_loop(stack)\n\n    def _run_bootstrap_loop(self, stack: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Run the iterative DFS bootstrap loop over a pre-built work stack.\n\n        Pops items one at a time, dispatches each phase, and pushes any\n        follow-on items (continuations and new dependencies) back onto the\n        stack. Updates the progress bar as items complete.\n\n        Args:\n            stack: Initial list of ``Phase`` objects to process. Modified\n                in-place; empty on return.\n        \"\"\"\n        while stack:\n            self._record_stack_state(stack)\n            item = stack.pop()\n            self.why = list(item.work_item.why_snapshot)\n\n            with (\n                req_ctxvar_context(item.work_item.req, item.work_item.resolved_version),\n                self._track_why(item),\n            ):\n                if item.requires_exclusive_run:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s requires exclusive build, draining background pool\",\n                        item.work_item.req,\n                    )\n                    self._drain_background_pool()\n                try:\n                    new_items = item.run(self)\n                except Exception as err:\n                    new_items = self._handle_phase_error(item, err)\n\n            new_dep_count = sum(1 for it in new_items if isinstance(it, Resolve))\n            if new_dep_count > 0:\n                self.progressbar.update_total(new_dep_count)\n            if not new_items:\n                self.progressbar.update()\n\n            self._push_items(stack, new_items)\n\n    def _bootstrap_one(self, req: Requirement, req_type: RequirementType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap a single requirement using an iterative DFS loop.\n\n        Internal method used only by the git URL resolution path\n        (``_handle_build_requirements``). All other callers should use\n        ``bootstrap(requirements)`` instead.\n\n        Uses an explicit LIFO stack instead of recursion to handle arbitrarily\n        deep dependency graphs without hitting Python's recursion limit.\n\n        In test mode, catches build exceptions, records package name, and continues.\n        In normal mode, raises exceptions immediately (fail-fast).\n\n        When multiple_versions is enabled, bootstraps all matching versions instead\n        of just the highest version.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(f\"bootstrapping {req} as {req_type} dependency of {self.why[-1:]}\")\n\n        # Capture parent from current why stack before creating work items\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None = None\n        if self.why:\n            _, parent_req, parent_version = self.why[-1]\n            parent = (parent_req, parent_version)\n\n        # Save the why stack so we can restore it after the iterative loop\n        # (the loop modifies self.why for each work item)\n        saved_why = list(self.why)\n\n        # Single RESOLVE item — resolution, version expansion, and error\n        # handling all happen inside the loop via Resolve.run().\n        initial_item = Resolve(\n            WorkItem(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                why_snapshot=list(self.why),\n                parent=parent,\n            )\n        )\n        stack: list[Phase] = []\n        self._push_items(stack, [initial_item])\n\n        self._run_bootstrap_loop(stack)\n\n        # empty the stack state file to show watchers are are done\n        # with bootstrapping\n        self._record_stack_state([])\n\n        # Restore why stack for the caller\n        self.why = saved_why\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def _track_why(\n        self,\n        item: Phase,\n    ) -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n        \"\"\"Context manager to track dependency chain in self.why stack.\n\n        No-op for phases where tracks_why is False (RESOLVE and START).\n        For all other phases, pushes the item onto the why stack and\n        ensures it is popped even if an exception occurs.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not item.tracks_why:\n            yield\n            return\n        wi = item.work_item\n        assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n        self.why.append((wi.req_type, wi.req, wi.resolved_version))\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            self.why.pop()\n\n    def record_test_mode_failure(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: str | None,\n        err: Exception,\n        failure_type: FailureType,\n        log_level: typing.Literal[\"error\", \"warning\"] = \"error\",\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Record a failure in test mode. Call this after checking test_mode.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement that failed.\n            version: The version being processed (None if not yet resolved).\n            err: The exception that was raised.\n            failure_type: Category of failure for analysis.\n            log_level: Log at error (fatal) or warning (non-fatal, continuing).\n        \"\"\"\n        version_str = f\"=={version}\" if version else \"\"\n        msg = f\"test mode: {failure_type} failed for {req.name}{version_str}\"\n        if log_level == \"warning\":\n            logger.warning(\"%s: %s (continuing)\", msg, err)\n        else:\n            logger.error(\"%s: %s\", msg, err, exc_info=True)\n\n        self.failed_packages.append(\n            {\n                \"package\": str(req.name),\n                \"version\": version,\n                \"exception_type\": err.__class__.__name__,\n                \"exception_message\": str(err),\n                \"failure_type\": failure_type,\n            }\n        )\n\n    @property\n    def explain(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Return message formatting current version of why stack.\"\"\"\n        return \" for \".join(\n            f\"{req_type} dependency {req} ({resolved_version})\"\n            for req_type, req, resolved_version in reversed(self.why)\n        )\n\n    def _prepare_build_dependencies(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version | None,\n        sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n        build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment,\n    ) -> set[Requirement]:\n        \"\"\"Prepare build dependencies for a package.\n\n        Only used by the git URL resolution path\n        (_resolve_version_from_git_url -> _get_version_from_package_metadata).\n        The main iterative bootstrap loop handles build deps via phase handlers.\n        \"\"\"\n        # build system\n        build_system_dependencies = dependencies.get_build_system_dependencies(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n        )\n        self._handle_build_requirements(\n            req,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM,\n            build_system_dependencies,\n        )\n            # converted to JSON without help.\n            json.dump(self._build_stack, f, indent=2, default=str)\n\n    def _record_stack_state(self, stack: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Write the current bootstrap stack to `self._stack_filename`.\n\n        Index 0 in the output corresponds to `stack[-1]`, the next item to be\n        processed. Overwrites the file on each call.\n        \"\"\"\n        records = [item.as_json() for item in reversed(stack)]\n        with open(self._stack_filename, \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(records, f, indent=2, default=str)\n\n    # ---- Iterative bootstrap: phase handlers and helpers ----\n\n    def _push_items(self, stack: list[Phase], items: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Push items onto the stack and submit background tasks in LIFO order.\n\n        Submits the item that will be processed first (top of stack) to the\n        background pool first, maximising overlap between background I/O and\n        main-thread serial work.\n        \"\"\"\n        stack.extend(items)\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            for item in reversed(items):\n                bg_work = item.background_work(self)\n                if bg_work is not None:\n                    item.bg_future = self._bg_pool.submit(bg_work)\n\n    def _drain_background_pool(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drain all in-flight background tasks and recreate the pool.\n\n        Used as an exclusive-build barrier: ensures all background I/O completes\n        before an exclusive build starts. ``cancel_futures=False`` guarantees\n        every submitted task runs to completion.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._bg_pool is not None:\n            self._bg_pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=False)\n            self._bg_pool = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(\n                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix=\"fromager-bg\"\n            )\n\n    def create_unresolved_work_items(\n        self,\n        deps: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n        dep_req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement,\n        parent_version: Version,\n    ) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"Create RESOLVE-phase work items for dependencies.\n\n        Called inside a parent's _track_why context so that why_snapshot\n        captures the parent's dependency chain. Resolution and error\n        handling happen later when each item's RESOLVE phase runs.\n        \"\"\"\n        return [\n            Resolve(\n                WorkItem(\n                    req=dep,\n                    req_type=dep_req_type,\n                    why_snapshot=list(self.why),\n                    parent=(parent_req, parent_version),\n                )\n            )\n            for dep in self._sort_requirements(deps)\n        ]\n\n    def _resolve_build_system_versions_by_name(\n        self,\n        build_system_deps: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system versions by looking up graph nodes.\n\n        Used by the git URL path where the parent node may not yet exist\n        in the dependency graph.\n        \"\"\"\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for dep in build_system_deps:\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            nodes = self.ctx.dependency_graph.get_nodes_by_name(str(dep_name))\n            for node in nodes:\n                if node.version in dep.specifier:\n                    resolved[dep_name] = (node.version, node.download_url)\n                    break\n        return resolved\n\n    def get_resolved_build_system_versions(\n        self,\n        item: WorkItem,\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system dependency versions.\n\n        Looks up the parent node's ``BUILD_SYSTEM`` edges in the dependency\n        graph to find what versions were resolved for each build-system\n        dependency.\n\n        Returns:\n            Mapping of canonicalized package name to ``(version, download_url)``.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert item.resolved_version is not None\n        parent_key = f\"{canonicalize_name(item.req.name)}=={item.resolved_version}\"\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

prompt: "This is the fromager repository (Python wheel builder). A virtualenv with the project\nand test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with\n`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts=\"\" tests/...`.\n\nImplement the following change to the resolver's max-release-age handling\n(`src/fromager/resolver.py`, `find_all_matching_from_provider()`, and its callers in\n`src/fromager/bootstrap_requirement_resolver.py`).\n\n1. Replace the boolean `fallback_on_empty_age_filter` parameter of\n   `find_all_matching_from_provider()` with an `AgeFallback` enum (exported from\n   `fromager.resolver`) selecting what happens when age filtering removes every candidate:\n   - `AgeFallback.ALL`: keep every candidate (this is the single-version default and the\n     current behaviour, including its \"keeping all to avoid empty resolution\" warning)\n   - `AgeFallback.NEWEST`: keep only the single newest candidate (new)\n   - `AgeFallback.NONE`: return an empty list\n   Name the new keyword\
  \ parameter `age_fallback`, default `AgeFallback.ALL`.\n   Log on the `fromager.resolver` logger when the fallback triggers, with these exact\n   messages (`%s`/`%d` formatting, `name` is `req.name`):\n   - ALL, warning: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days, keeping all to avoid empty resolution\"`\n   - NEWEST, info: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days, falling back to newest version %s\"`\n   - NONE, info: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days\"`\n   Multi-version bootstrap mode must use `AgeFallback.NEWEST`, so that when a dependency\n   has no release inside the age window (bar from two years ago depended on by a recent\n   foo) its newest version is built instead of failing, which avoids cascading failures\n   in the dependent package.\n\n2. Packages whose constraint pins an exact version (the provider's `constraints` object\n   returns a constraint for the requirement name and that constraint is a single `==`\n   specifier)\
  \ skip age filtering entirely. A pin is explicit user intent and must not be\n   overridden by the age heuristic. Range constraints (`>=`, `<`, `!=`, ...) are still\n   age-filtered like unconstrained packages. Log at INFO on the\n   `fromager.resolver` logger: `\"%s: skipping age filter for pinned constraint (%d candidate(s))\"`.\n   Previously, in multi-version mode a constrained package pinned to a version older than\n   the window lost every candidate and resolution failed silently; in single-version mode\n   the fallback kept all candidates but logged the misleading warning.\n\nUpdate docstrings, add tests in `tests/test_cooldown.py` and\n`tests/test_bootstrap_requirement_resolver.py`, and run both files.\n"

"""Requirement resolution for bootstrap process.

Handles PyPI and graph-based resolution strategies.
Git URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper (orchestration concern).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels
from .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from .requirements_file import RequirementType

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class BootstrapRequirementResolver:
    """Resolve package requirements from PyPI or dependency graph during bootstrap.

    Single Responsibility: Coordinate resolution strategies for bootstrap process.
    Reason to Change: Resolution algorithm or provider priorities change.

    Resolution strategies (in order):
    1. Previous dependency graph (if available)
    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)

    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper
    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize requirement resolver.

        Args:
            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings
            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching
            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through
                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the
                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other
                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.
            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.
                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.
        """
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url
        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution
        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types
        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.
        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)
        # Value: {version: url}
        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}
        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.
        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)
        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.
        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()
        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def resolve(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,
        pre_built: bool | None = None,
        return_all_versions: bool = False,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:
        """Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).

        Uses a two-step strategy:
        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch
           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the
           package-level known-versions cache.
        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current
           requirement specifier.

        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,
        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups
        with different specifiers for the same package.

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            req_type: Type of requirement
            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain
            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).
                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.
            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,
                return only the highest matching version.

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).
            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching
            versions when return_all_versions=True.

        """
        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key)
        if pre_built is None:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            pre_built = pbi.pre_built

        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)

        with self._lock:
            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:
                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and
                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.
                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)
                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)
            else:
                logger.debug(f"rule already resolved: {req}")

            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.
            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)

        if not matching:
            return []
        if return_all_versions:
            return matching
        return [matching[0]]

    def get_cached_resolution(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        pre_built: bool,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:
        """Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.

        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing
        callers to distinguish between "no matching versions" and "not yet resolved".

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.
        """
        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)
        with self._lock:
            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:
                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)
        return None

    def _resolve_and_extend(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        pre_built: bool,
        parent_req: Requirement | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Resolve versions from graph/network and extend known versions cache."""
        # Try previous dependency graph
        cached_resolution = self._resolve_from_graph(
            req=req,
            req_type=req_type,
            pre_built=pre_built,
            parent_req=parent_req,
        )

        if cached_resolution:
            logger.debug(
                f"resolved from previous bootstrap: {len(cached_resolution)} version(s)"
            )
            results = cached_resolution
        elif pre_built:
            # Resolve prebuilt wheel
            wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(
                self.ctx, req, cache_wheel_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL
            )
            results = wheels.resolve_all_prebuilt_wheels(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,
                req_type=req_type,
            )
        else:
            # Resolve source (sdist)
            provider = sources.get_source_provider(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                sdist_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL,
                req_type=req_type,
            )

# Based on https://github.com/sarugaku/resolvelib/blob/main/examples/pypi_wheel_provider.py
#
# Modified to look at sdists instead of wheels and to avoid trying to
# resolve any dependencies.

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import enum
import functools
import logging
import os
import re
import typing
from collections.abc import Iterable
from operator import attrgetter
from platform import python_version
from urllib.parse import quote, urlparse

import pypi_simple
import resolvelib
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.specifiers import InvalidSpecifier, SpecifierSet
from packaging.tags import Tag, sys_tags
from packaging.utils import (
    BuildTag,
    canonicalize_name,
    parse_wheel_filename,
)
from packaging.version import Version

from . import overrides
from .candidate import Candidate, Cooldown
from .constraints import Constraints

from .extras_provider import ExtrasProvider
from .http_retry import RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS, retry_on_exception
from .request_session import session

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class AgeFallback(enum.Enum):
    """Select the fallback when max-release-age removes every candidate."""

    ALL = "all"
    NEWEST = "newest"
    NONE = "none"

PYTHON_VERSION = Version(python_version())
DEBUG_RESOLVER = os.environ.get("DEBUG_RESOLVER", "")
PYPI_SERVER_URL = "https://pypi.org/simple"
GITHUB_URL = "https://github.com"

# all supported tags
SUPPORTED_TAGS: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(sys_tags())
# same, but ignore the platform for 'ignore_platform' flag
IGNORE_PLATFORM: str = "ignore"
SUPPORTED_TAGS_IGNORE_PLATFORM: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(
    Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS
)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )

validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n """Tests for bootstrap_requirement_resolver module."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import resolver
from fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver import BootstrapRequirementResolver
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

# Test fixture: previous dependency graph
old_graph = DependencyGraph()

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("foo"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("foo"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
    req_version=Version("7"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("bar"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("bar"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
    req_version=Version("6"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("blah"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("blah"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
    req_version=Version("5"),
)


def test_resolve_from_graph_no_changes(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves from previous graph with no changes."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Resolving new dependency that doesn't exist in graph
    assert (
        resolver._resolve_from_graph(
            req=Requirement("xyz"),
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            pre_built=False,
            parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
        )
        is None
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("7"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_upgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver prefers top-level requirements over history."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr==8
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr==8"),
        req_version=Version("8"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - should get upgraded version from top-level
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("8"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - constraint prevents upgrade
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_downgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver handles version downgrades from top-level requirements."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr<=6
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr<=6"),
        req_version=Version("6"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - gets downgraded to 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - already at 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_toplevel_dep(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves top-level dependencies correctly."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement for foo
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(

    )

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of bar (no change)
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_missing_timestamp_error_message() -> None:
    """Resolution failure due to missing timestamps produces a clear error message."""
    no_timestamp_response = {
        "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
        "name": "test-pkg",
        "files": [
            {
                "filename": "test_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
                "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
                "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            },
        ],
    }

"""PackageBuildInfo class and system resource helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import pathlib
import types
import typing
from collections.abc import Mapping

import psutil
from packaging.utils import BuildTag, NormalizedName
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import overrides, threading_utils
from ._models import (
    GitOptions,
    PackageSettings,
    ProjectOverride,
    PurlConfig,
    VariantInfo,
)
from ._templates import _resolve_template, substitute_template
from ._typedefs import Annotations, PackageVersion, PatchMap, Template, Variant

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .. import build_environment
    from ._settings import Settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _default_is_pre_built(*, version: Version, variant: Variant) -> None:
    """Defer the pre-built decision to package settings."""
    return None


def get_available_memory_gib() -> float:
    """available virtual memory in GiB"""
    return psutil.virtual_memory().available / (1024**3)


class PackageBuildInfo:
    """Package build information

    Public API for PackageSettings with i
    """

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, ps: PackageSettings) -> None:
        self._variant = typing.cast(Variant, settings.variant)
        self._patches_dir = settings.patches_dir
        self._variant_changelog = settings.variant_changelog()
        self._max_jobs: int | None = settings.max_jobs
        self._ps = ps
        self._plugin_module: types.ModuleType | typing.Literal[False] | None = False
        self._patches: PatchMap | None = None
        self._annotations: Annotations | None = None

    @property
    def package(self) -> NormalizedName:
        """Package name"""
        return typing.cast(NormalizedName, self._ps.name)

    @property
    def variant(self) -> Variant:
        """Variant name"""
        return self._variant

    @property
    def purl_config(self) -> PurlConfig | None:
        """Per-package purl configuration for SBOM generation."""
        return self._ps.purl

    @property
    def annotations(self) -> Annotations:
        """Get Package and variant annotations

        Annotations can be used to attach arbitrary metadata to packages and
        package variants. The feature is inspired by Kubernetes's
        annotations. Variant keys have a higher precedence than package keys.

        The prefix ``fromager.`` is reserved for future use by Fromager.

        ::

           annotations:
             "downstream.maintainer": "Platform Team"
           variants:
             cuda:
               annotations:
                 "downstream.maintainer": "CUDA Accelerator Team"
        """
        if self._annotations is None:
            vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)
            va = vi.annotations if vi is not None else None
            self._annotations = Annotations(self._ps.annotations, va)
        return self._annotations

    @property
    def plugin(self) -> types.ModuleType | None:
        """Get Fromager plugin module"""
        if self._plugin_module is False:
            exts = overrides._get_extensions()
            try:
                mod = exts[self.override_module_name].plugin
                self._plugin_module = typing.cast(types.ModuleType, mod)
            except KeyError:
                self._plugin_module = None
        return self._plugin_module

    def get_all_patches(self) -> PatchMap:
        """Get a mapping of version to list of patches"""

        if self._patches is None:
            patches: PatchMap = {}
            version: Version | None

            # Find unversioned and versioned directories (name + '-' + version)
            # with patches for the package.
            dirs_to_scan = []
            unversioned_dir = self._patches_dir / self.override_module_name
            if unversioned_dir.exists():
                dirs_to_scan.append(unversioned_dir)
            versioned_pattern = f"{self.override_module_name}-*"
            dirs_to_scan.extend(self._patches_dir.glob(versioned_pattern))

            prefix_len = len(self.override_module_name) + 1
            for patchdir in dirs_to_scan:
                if patchdir.name == self.override_module_name:
                    version = None
                else:
                    version = Version(patchdir.name[prefix_len:])
                patches[version] = list(patchdir.glob("*.patch"))
                # variant-specific patches
                patches[version].extend(patchdir.joinpath(self.variant).glob("*.patch"))
                patches[version].sort(key=lambda p: p.name)

            self._patches = patches
        return self._patches

    def get_patches(self, version: Version) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
        """Get patches for a version (and unversioned patches)"""
        # ignore local version for patches
        version = Version(version.public)
        patchfiles: list[pathlib.Path] = []
        patchmap = self.get_all_patches()
        # unversioned patches
        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(None, []))
        # version-specific patches
        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(version, []))
        # sort by basename
        patchfiles.sort(key=lambda p: p.name)
        return patchfiles

    @property
    def has_config(self) -> bool:
        """Does the package have a config file?"""
        return self._ps.has_config

    @property
    def has_customizations(self) -> bool:
        """Does the package have any customizations?"""
        return bool(
            self.has_config or self.plugin is not None or self.get_all_patches()
        )

    @property
    def pre_built(self) -> bool:
        """Does the variant use pre-build wheels?"""
        return self.is_pre_built()

    def is_pre_built(self, version: Version | None = None) -> bool:
        """Version-aware pre-built check.

        Resolution order:

        1. Plugin hook ``is_pre_built`` (if version given and hook exists)
        2. Version-specific YAML setting
        3. Variant-wide default

        .. versionadded:: 0.95.0
        """
        vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)
        if vi is None:
            return False
        if version is not None:
            result = overrides.find_and_invoke(
                self.package,
                "is_pre_built",
                _default_is_pre_built,
                version=version,
                variant=self.variant,
            )
            if result is not None:
                return bool(result)
            pv = typing.cast(PackageVersion, Version(version.public))
            vs = vi.versions.get(pv)
            if vs is not None and vs.pre_built is not None:
                return vs.pre_built

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import context as context_module
from .. import resolver, sources, wheels

from ..requirements_file import RequirementType
from ._phase import Phase
from ._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from ._types import BootstrapPhase

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from ._bootstrapper import Bootstrapper

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _re_resolve_url(
    ctx: context_module.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType,
    resolved_version: Version,
    pre_built: bool,
    cache_wheel_server_url: str | None,
) -> str | None:
    """Resolve the URL for a pinned version using its effective source type."""
    pinned_req = Requirement(f"{req.name}=={resolved_version}")
    if pre_built:
        wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(
            ctx,
            req,
            cache_wheel_server_url=cache_wheel_server_url,
            version=resolved_version,
        )
        try:
            url, _ = wheels.resolve_prebuilt_wheel(
                ctx=ctx,
                req=pinned_req,
                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,
                req_type=req_type,
            )
        except ExceptionGroup:
            return None
        return str(url)

    pbi = ctx.package_build_info(req)
    provider = sources.get_source_provider(
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        sdist_server_url=pbi.resolver_sdist_server_url(resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL),
        req_type=req_type,
    )
    results = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(provider, pinned_req)
    return str(results[0][0]) if results else None


class Start(Phase):
    """Record a resolved requirement in the dependency graph and deduplicate.

    Adds the ``(parent → req)`` edge to the dependency graph, then checks
    whether this ``(req, version)`` pair has already been processed.  Duplicate
    requirements are silently dropped; new ones proceed to source preparation.
    ``tracks_why`` is ``False`` so graph additions happen before the why-stack
    is updated.

    Next phase: ``PrepareSource`` (new requirement) or ``[]`` (already seen).
    """

    phase: typing.ClassVar[BootstrapPhase] = BootstrapPhase.START
    tracks_why: typing.ClassVar[bool] = False

    def run(self, bt: Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:
        """START phase: add to graph, check if already seen.

        _track_why is a no-op for this phase (tracks_why is False),
        matching the original behavior where graph addition and
        seen-check happen before pushing onto the why stack.

        Returns:
            Empty list if already seen (nothing to do).
            [PrepareSource] if this is new work.
        """
        wi = self.work_item
        assert wi.resolved_version is not None
        assert wi.source_url is not None

        pbi = bt.ctx.package_build_info(wi.req)
        wi.pbi_pre_built = pbi.is_pre_built(wi.resolved_version)
        wi.exclusive_build = pbi.exclusive_build
        if wi.pbi_pre_built != pbi.pre_built or (
            wi.pbi_pre_built
            and pbi.get_wheel_server_url(wi.resolved_version) != pbi.wheel_server_url
        ):
            logger.info(
                "re-resolving URL for %s==%s as %s",
                wi.req.name,
                wi.resolved_version,
                "pre-built wheel" if wi.pbi_pre_built else "source distribution",
            )
            resolved_url = _re_resolve_url(
                bt.ctx,
                wi.req,
                wi.req_type,
                wi.resolved_version,
                wi.pbi_pre_built,
                bt.cache_wheel_server_url,
            )
            if resolved_url is None:
                logger.warning(
                    "could not re-resolve URL for %s==%s; keeping %s",
                    wi.req.name,
                    wi.resolved_version,
                    wi.source_url,
                )
            else:
                wi.source_url = resolved_url

        # Add to graph (skip TOP_LEVEL, already added in _resolve_and_add_top_level)
        if wi.req_type != RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL:
            bt.add_to_graph(
                wi.req,
                wi.req_type,
                wi.resolved_version,
                wi.source_url,
                wi.parent,
            )

        wi.build_sdist_only = bt.sdist_only and not wi.is_build_requirement_context()

        if bt.has_been_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only):
            logger.debug(
                f"redundant {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} "
                f"({wi.resolved_version}, sdist_only={wi.build_sdist_only}) "
                f"for {bt.explain}"
            )
            return []
        bt.mark_as_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only)

        logger.info(
            f"new {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} resolves to {wi.resolved_version}"
        )

        return [PrepareSource(wi)]

Hooks and Overrides
===================

Fromager has two plugin systems that serve different purposes:
**per-package overrides** replace default behavior for a specific
package, while **global hooks** broadcast notifications after events
for every package.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.
   :doc:`/reference/hooks` documents each override hook's arguments and
   return values.  :doc:`/customization` covers global hooks with code
   examples.

Comparison
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 20 40 40

   * - Aspect
     - Per-Package Overrides
     - Global Hooks
   * - **Scope**
     - One named package
     - Every package
   * - **Cardinality**
     - At most one override module per package
     - Multiple plugins per hook
   * - **Semantics**
     - Replaces the default implementation
     - Runs in addition to the default
   * - **Return value**
     - Used by the caller
     - None (fire-and-forget)
   * - **Typical use**
     - Custom download, build, or resolution logic
     - Publishing wheels, validation, logging

Per-Package Overrides
---------------------

An override module provides alternative implementations for specific
build steps.  Fromager looks up the module by the canonicalized package
name.  If the module defines the requested method, it is called instead
of the default; otherwise the default runs.

Override hooks cover resolution, source acquisition, building,
dependency extraction, and build environment customization.  Third-party
packages register overrides via the ``fromager.project_overrides``
entry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a package name to
a Python module.

See :doc:`/reference/hooks` for the complete list of hooks and their
arguments.

The ``is_pre_built`` override is consulted for version-specific checks.
Its non-``None`` result takes precedence over version and variant YAML
settings; returning ``None`` defers to those settings. The variant default
property does not invoke this hook.

Global Hooks
------------

Global hooks are event callbacks that fire for every package.  All
registered plugins for a hook are called sequentially.  They cannot
alter the build result — they are purely side-effecting notifications.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Hook
     - When it fires
   * - ``post_build``
     - After a wheel is built from source (not for prebuilt wheels)
   * - ``prebuilt_wheel``
     - After a prebuilt wheel is downloaded (not built from source)
   * - ``post_bootstrap``
     - After a package is bootstrapped, before its install dependencies
       are processed

Third-party packages register hooks via the ``fromager.hooks``
entry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a hook name to
a callable.

See :doc:`/customization` for examples and argument details.
