Package Settings
================

Fromager uses a layered settings system to configure how each package
is resolved, downloaded, patched, and built.  Settings flow from YAML
files on disk through a merge pipeline into a single facade object
used by the build pipeline.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`/reference/config-reference` documents every configuration
   field.  :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.

Settings Loading Flow
---------------------

.. code-block:: text

   CLI flags
   (--settings-file, --settings-dir, --patches-dir)
         │
         ▼
   Settings.from_files()
   ├── Load settings.yaml ──► SettingsFile (global config)
   └── Glob settings/*.yaml ──► PackageSettings (one per package)
         │
         ▼
   Settings object (held by WorkContext)
         │
         │  package_build_info("torch")  (on demand, cached)
         ▼
   PackageBuildInfo
   (single facade used by the build pipeline)

``PackageBuildInfo`` objects are created lazily the first time a
package is queried and cached for the rest of the run.

Directory Structure
-------------------

.. code-block:: text

   overrides/
   ├── settings.yaml              # Global settings
   ├── settings/                  # Per-package settings
   │   ├── torch.yaml
   │   ├── flash-attn.yaml
   │   └── ...
   └── patches/                   # Patches
       ├── torch/                 # Unversioned (all versions)
       │   ├── 001-fix.patch
       │   └── cpu/               # Variant-specific
       │       └── 002-cpu.patch
       └── torch-2.4.0/           # Version-specific
           └── 001-ver.patch

Package YAML filenames use the canonicalized package name (lowercase,
hyphens).  All three directories are configurable via CLI flags.

Merge Order
-----------

Settings are merged from least-specific to most-specific.  Later
layers override earlier ones:

.. code-block:: text

   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  1. Pydantic field defaults                      │
   │     (empty env, default build options, etc.)     │
   │                                                  │
   │  2. Global settings.yaml                         │
   │     (SBOM config, global changelog)              │
   │                                                  │
   │  3. Per-package YAML file                        │
   │     (env, resolver, build options, patches, ...) │
   │                                                  │
   │  4. Variant overrides (within package YAML)      │
   │     (env vars, pre_built, wheel_server_url)      │
   │                                                  │
   │  5. Version-specific patches and changelog       │
   │     (patches/<pkg>-<version>/, changelog entries)│
   │                                                  │
   │  6. Override plugin hooks (runtime)              │
   │     (update_extra_environ can mutate env vars)   │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

For environment variables specifically, the merge order within a
single ``get_extra_environ()`` call is: parallel-jobs settings, build
environment paths, package-level ``env``, then variant-level ``env``.
Entries can reference earlier values using ``$VAR`` template syntax.

PackageBuildInfo Facade
-----------------------

``PackageBuildInfo`` is the single interface the build pipeline uses to
query all package configuration.  It wraps a ``PackageSettings`` and
adds variant awareness, patch discovery, and template resolution.

Variant settings can override ``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url`` for
individual versions under ``variants.<variant>.versions``. The bootstrapper
uses those effective settings to re-resolve the pinned source or wheel URL
before recording the dependency graph edge.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Category
     - What it provides
   * - **Identity**
     - Package name, variant, whether a config file exists, override
       plugin module
   * - **Resolution**
     - Sdist server URL, include wheels/sdists flags, platform
       filtering, per-package cooldown override
   * - **Build config**
     - Environment variables, parallel jobs, exclusive build flag,
       PEP 517 config settings, build directory
   * - **Source**
     - Download URL and filename templates with ``${version}``
       substitution, git submodule options
   * - **Patches**
     - Merged list of unversioned + version-specific + variant-specific
       patch files, sorted by filename
   * - **Metadata**
     - Build tag (from changelog length), annotations, PURL config,
       pyproject.toml overrides

See :doc:`/reference/config-reference` for the full field reference.

Use normal punctuation or connective words instead.\n- Use module-level Python imports unless a function-level import is necessary to\n  avoid a circular dependency.\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. This guide summarizes how to set up a workspace, follow our standards, and submit polished changes. Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for Variant keys have a higher precedence than package keys.\n\n        The prefix ``fromager.`` is reserved for future use by Fromager.\n\n        ::\n\n           annotations:\n             \"downstream.maintainer\": \"Platform Team\"\n           variants:\n             cuda:\n               annotations:\n                 \"downstream.maintainer\": \"CUDA Accelerator Team\"\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._annotations is None:\n            vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)\n            va = vi.annotations if vi is not None else None\n            self._annotations = Annotations(self._ps.annotations, va)\n        return self._annotations\n\n    @property\n    def plugin(self) -> types.ModuleType | None:\n        \"\"\"Get Fromager plugin module\"\"\"\n        if self._plugin_module is False:\n            exts = overrides._get_extensions()\n            try:\n                mod = exts[self.override_module_name].plugin\n                self._plugin_module = typing.cast(types.ModuleType, mod)\n            except KeyError:\n                self._plugin_module = None\n        return self._plugin_module\n\n    def get_all_patches(self) -> PatchMap:\n        \"\"\"Get a mapping of version to list of patches\"\"\"\n\n        if self._patches is None:\n            patches: PatchMap = {}\n            version: Version | None\n\n            # Find unversioned and versioned directories (name + '-' + version)\n            # with patches for the package.\n            dirs_to_scan = []\n            unversioned_dir = self._patches_dir / self.override_module_name\n            if unversioned_dir.exists():\n                dirs_to_scan.append(unversioned_dir)\n            versioned_pattern = f\"{self.override_module_name}-*\"\n            dirs_to_scan.extend(self._patches_dir.glob(versioned_pattern))\n\n            prefix_len = len(self.override_module_name) + 1\n            for patchdir in dirs_to_scan:\n                if patchdir.name == self.override_module_name:\n                    version = None\n                else:\n                    version = Version(patchdir.name[prefix_len:])\n                patches[version] = list(patchdir.glob(\"*.patch\"))\n                # variant-specific patches\n                patches[version].extend(patchdir.joinpath(self.variant).glob(\"*.patch\"))\n                patches[version].sort(key=lambda p: p.name)\n\n            self._patches = patches\n        return self._patches\n\n    def get_patches(self, version: Version) -> list[pathlib.Path]:\n        \"\"\"Get patches for a version (and unversioned patches)\"\"\"\n        # ignore local version for patches\n        version = Version(version.public)\n        patchfiles: list[pathlib.Path] = []\n        patchmap = self.get_all_patches()\n        # unversioned patches\n        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(None, []))\n        # version-specific patches\n        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(version, []))\n        # sort by basename\n        patchfiles.sort(key=lambda p: p.name)\n        return patchfiles\n\n    @property\n    def has_config(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Does the package have a config file?\"\"\"\n        return self._ps.has_config\n\n    @property\n    def has_customizations(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Does the package have any customizations?\"\"\"\n        return bool(\n            self.has_config or self.plugin is not None or self.get_all_patches()\n        )\n\n    @property\n    def pre_built(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Does the variant use pre-build wheels?\"\"\"\n        vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)\n        if vi is not None:\n            return vi.pre_built\n        return False\n\n    def is_pre_built(self, version: Version | None = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Version-aware pre-built check.\n\n        Resolution order:\n\n        1. Plugin hook ``is_pre_built`` (if version given and hook exists)\n        2. Version-specific YAML setting\n        3. Variant-wide default\n\n        .. versionadded:: 0.90.0\n        \"\"\"\n        vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)\n        if vi is None:\n            return False\n        if version is not hook_fn, version=version, variant=self.variant\n                )\n                if result is not None:\n                    return bool(result)\n            pv = typing.cast(PackageVersion, version)\n            vs = vi.versions.get(pv)\n            if vs is not None and vs.pre_built is not None:\n                return vs.pre_built\n        return vi.pre_built\n\n    @property\n    def wheel_server_url(self) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Alternative package index for pre-build wheel\"\"\"\n        vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)\n        if vi is not None and vi.wheel_server_url is not None:\n            return str(vi.wheel_server_url)\n        return None\n\n    def get_wheel_server_url(self, version: Version | None = None) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Version-aware wheel server URL.\n\n        Returns the version-specific URL if defined, otherwise\n        falls back to the variant-wide default.\n\n        .. versionadded:: 0.90.0\n        \"\"\"\n        vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)\n        if vi is None:\n            return None\n        if version is not None:\n            pv = typing.cast(PackageVersion, version)\n per-package in the package settings file.\n    \"\"\"\n\n\n# Environment variable filter patterns for ExternalCommands.\n# Pattern: starts with letter or underscore, rest is letters/digits/underscores,\n# optionally ending with ``*`` (trailing wildcard).\n# DeleteEnvPattern additionally allows bare ``*`` (catch-all).\nKeepEnvPattern = typing.Annotated[\n    str,\n    StringConstraints(pattern=r\"^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\\*?$\"),\n]\n\nDeleteEnvPattern = typing.Annotated[\n    str,\n    StringConstraints(pattern=r\"^(\\*|[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\\*?)$\"),\n]\n\n\n# POSIX.1-2024 sec. 8.1: environment variable names consist of uppercase\n# letters, digits, and underscores and do not begin with a digit.  We\n# also accept lowercase letters for portability (common on Linux).\n_POSIX_ENV_KEY_RE = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\")\n\n\ndef _compile_env_patterns(\n    patterns: tuple[str, ...],\n    *,\n    case_insensitive: bool = False,\n) -> re.Pattern[str]:\n    \"\"\"Compile env filter patterns into a single regex for ``fullmatch``.\n\n    Exact patterns (e.g. ``HOME``) become ``HOME`` and prefix patterns\n    (e.g. ``LC_*``) become ``LC_.*``.  The result is\n    ``HOME|LC_.*|...`` (used with ``fullmatch``).\n\n    *patterns* must be non-empty.\n    \"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for p in patterns:\n        if p.endswith(\"*\"):\n            parts.append(re.escape(p[:-1]) + \".*\")\n        else:\n            parts.append(re.escape(p))\n    flags = re.IGNORECASE if case_insensitive else 0\n    return re.compile(\"|\".join(parts), flags)\n\n\nclass ExternalCommands(pydantic.BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Environment variable filtering for subprocesses.\n\n    Variables whose keys are not valid POSIX names are always removed.\n    A hard-coded set of variables required for basic subprocess\n    operation (see ``DEFAULT_KEEP_ENV``) is always kept.  User-supplied\n    ``keep_env`` patterns are evaluated before ``delete_env`` patterns.\n\n    ::\n\n      external_commands:\n        keep_env:\n          - \"CARGO_*\"\n        delete_env:\n          - \"CI_TOKEN\"\n          - \"AWS_*\"\n\n    .. versionadded:: 0.92.0\n    \"\"\"\n\n    model_config = MODEL_CONFIG\n\n    DEFAULT_KEEP_ENV: typing.ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = (\n        \"HOME\",\n        \"HOSTNAME\",\n        \"LANG\",\n        \"LANGUAGE\",\n        \"LC_*\",\n        \"LOGNAME\",\n        \"NO_COLOR\",\n        \"PATH\",\n        \"SHELL\",\n        \"TEMP\",\n        \"TERM\",\n        \"TMP\",\n        \"TMPDIR\",\n        \"TZ\",\n        \"USER\",\n    )\n    \"\"\"Patterns always kept regardless of user configuration.\"\"\"\n\n    keep_env: list[KeepEnvPattern] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    \"\"\"Allowlist patterns (evaluated before ``delete_env``)\"\"\"\n\n    delete_env: list[DeleteEnvPattern] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    \"\"\"Blocklist patterns (evaluated after ``keep_env``)\"\"\"\n\n    _keep_re: re.Pattern[str] | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)\n    _delete_re: re.Pattern[str] | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)\n\n    @pydantic.model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def validate_delete_env(self) -> typing.Self:\n        \"\"\"Validate ``delete_env`` for conflicts and redundancy.\"\"\"\n        if not self.delete_env:\n            return self\n        if \"*\" in self.delete_env and len(self.delete_env) > 1:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"delete_env: bare '*' must be the only entry, \"\n                \"additional patterns are redundant\"\n            )\n        # Exact string overlap check.  This catches obvious\n        # configuration mistakes (e.g. ``delete_env: [HOME]``) but does\n        # not detect all conflicts — for example ``delete_env: [LC_ALL]``\n        # is not flagged even though ``LC_ALL`` matches the default keep\n        # pattern ``LC_*``.\n        keep = set(self.DEFAULT_KEEP_ENV) | set(self.keep_env)\n        overlap = keep & set(self.delete_env)\n        if overlap:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"delete_env overlaps with keep_env / DEFAULT_KEEP_ENV: \"\n                f\"{sorted(overlap)}\"\n            )\n        return self\n\n    def model_post_init(self, __context: typing.Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Pydantic post init hook to initialize internal data structures\"\"\"\n        if self.delete_env:\n            self._keep_re = _compile_env_patterns(\n                self.DEFAULT_KEEP_ENV + tuple(self.keep_env)\n            )\n            if \"*\" not in self.delete_env:\n                self._delete_re = _compile_env_patterns(\n                    tuple(self.delete_env), case_insensitive=True\n                )\n\n    def filter_env(self, env: Mapping[str, str]) -> Mapping[str, str]:\n        \"\"\"Filter environment variables by keep/delete patterns.\n\n        Variables whose keys are not valid POSIX names are always\n        removed first. _keep_re is only set in model_post_init when delete_env is\n        # non-empty, so None means no filtering is configured.\n        if self._keep_re is None:\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport collections\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport pathlib\nimport shutil\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nimport typing\nimport zipfile\n\nimport elfdeps\nimport tomlkit\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.tags import Tag\nfrom packaging.utils import (\n    BuildTag,\n    parse_wheel_filename,\n)\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom . import (\n    dependencies,\n    downloads,\n    external_commands,\n    metrics,\n    overrides,\n    packagesettings,\n    requirements_file,\n    resolver,\n    sbom,\n)\nfrom .pkgmetadata.pep376 import verbatim_dist_name\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from . import build_environment, context\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nFROMAGER_BUILD_SETTINGS = \"fromager-build-settings\"\nFROMAGER_ELF_PROVIDES = \"fromager-elf-provides.txt\"\nFROMAGER_ELF_REQUIRES = \"fromager-elf-requires.txt\"\nFROMAGER_BUILD_REQ_PREFIX = \"fromager\"\n\n\ndef _log_existing_sboms(\n    req: Requirement,\n    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Log any existing SBOM files found in the wheel's .dist-info/sboms/ directory.\"\"\"\n    sboms_dir = dist_info_dir / \"sboms\"\n    if not sboms_dir.is_dir():\n        return\n    sbom_files = sorted(sboms_dir.iterdir())\n    if sbom_files:\n        names = [f.name for f in sbom_files]\n        logger.info(\n            \"%s: found existing SBOM files in wheel: %s\",\n            req.name,\n            \", \".join(names),\n        )\n\n\ndef _extra_metadata_elfdeps(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    wheel_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,\n) -> typing.Iterable[elfdeps.ELFInfo]:\n    \"\"\"Analyze a wheel's ELF dependencies and add info files\n\n    Logs and returns library dependencies and library provides. Writes\n    requirements to dist-info.\n    \"\"\"\n    # mapping of required libraries to list of versions\n    requires: set[elfdeps.SOInfo] = set()\n    provides: set[elfdeps.SOInfo] = set()\n    runpaths: set[str] = set()\n    elfinfos: list[elfdeps.ELFInfo] = []\n\n    settings = elfdeps.ELFAnalyzeSettings(filter_soname=True)\n    for info in elfdeps.analyze_dirtree(wheel_root_dir, settings=settings):\n        if info.filename is not None:\n            relname = str(info.filename.relative_to(wheel_root_dir))\n        else:\n            relname = \"n/a\"\n        logger.debug(\n            f\"{relname} ({info.soname}) \"\n            f\"requires {sorted(info.requires)}, \"\n            f\"provides {sorted(info.provides)}\"\n        )\n        provides.update(info.provides)\n        requires.update(info.requires)\n        if info.runpath is not None:\n            runpaths.update(info.runpath)\n        elfinfos.append(info)\n\n    # Don't list provided names as requirements\n    requires = requires.difference(provides)\n\n    if requires:\n        reqmap: dict[str, list[str]] = collections.defaultdict(list)\n        for r in requires:\n            reqmap[r.soname].append(r.version)\n\n        names = sorted(\n            name for name in reqmap if not name.startswith((\"ld-linux\", \"rtld\"))\n        )\n        logger.info(\"Requires libraries: %s\", \", \".join(names))\n        for name, versions in sorted(reqmap.items()):\n            logger.debug(\n                \"Requires %s(%s)\",\n                name,\n                \", \".join(v for v in versions if v),\n            )\n\n        requires_file = dist_info_dir / FROMAGER_ELF_REQUIRES\n        with requires_file.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n            for soinfo in sorted(requires):\n                f.write(f\"{soinfo}\\n\")\n\n    if provides:\n        names = sorted(p.soname for p in provides)\n        logger.info(\"Provides libraries: %s\", \", \".join(names))\n\n        provides_file = dist_info_dir / FROMAGER_ELF_PROVIDES\n        with provides_file.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n            for soinfo in sorted(provides):\n                f.write(f\"{soinfo}\\n\")\n\n    if runpaths:\n        logger.info(\"Libraries have runpath: %s\", \" \".join(sorted(runpaths)))\n\n    return elfinfos\n\n\ndef extract_info_from_wheel_file(\n parse_wheel_filename(wheel_file.name)\n    dist_name = verbatim_dist_name(wheel_file.name)\n    return (dist_name, version, build_tag, wheel_tags)\n\n\ndef default_add_extra_metadata_to_wheels(\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    version: Version,\n    extra_environ: dict[str, str],\n    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    dist_info_dir: pathlib.Path,\n) -> dict[str, typing.Any]:\n    \"\"\"Default implementation returns empty dict - no extra metadata.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n\n\n@metrics.timeit(description=\"add extra metadata to wheels\")\ndef add_extra_metadata_to_wheels(\n    *,\n    ctx: context.WorkContext,\n    req: Requirement,\n    version: Version,\n    extra_environ: dict[str, str],\n    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    wheel_file: pathlib.Path,\n) -> pathlib.Path:\n    \"\"\"Unpack a wheel, inject extra metadata, and repack with a build tag.\n\n    Unpacks the wheel, validates dist-info, adds plugin metadata, build\n    settings, requirement files, ELF dependency info (Linux only), and\n    an SBOM. Repacks with ``wheel pack`` and deletes the original.\n    \"\"\"\n    pbi = ctx.package_build_info(req)\n    dist_name, dist_version, _, wheel_tags = extract_info_from_wheel_file(\n        req, wheel_file\n    )\n    dist_filename = f\"{dist_name}-{dist_version}\"\n\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as dir_name:\n        wheel_root_dir = pathlib.Path(dir_name) / dist_filename\n        wheel_root_dir.mkdir()\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(str(wheel_file)) as zf:\n            for infolist in zf.filelist:\n                # Check for path traversal attempts\n                if (\n                    os.path.isabs(infolist.filename)\n                    or \"..\" in pathlib.Path(infolist.filename).parts\n                ):\n                    raise ValueError(f\"Unsafe path in wheel: {infolist.filename}\")\n                zf.extract(infolist, wheel_root_dir)\n                # the higher 16 bits store the permissions and type of file (i.e. stat.filemode)\n                # the lower bits of this give us the permission\n                permissions = infolist.external_attr >> 16 & 0o777\n                wheel_root_dir.joinpath(infolist.filename).chmod(permissions)\n\n        dist_info_dir = wheel_root_dir / f\"{dist_filename}.dist-info\"\n        if not dist_info_dir.is_dir():\n            raise ValueError(f\"{wheel_file} does not contain {dist_info_dir.name}\")\n\n        _log_existing_sboms(req, dist_info_dir)\n\n        data_to_add = overrides.find_and_invoke(\n            req.name,\n            \"add_extra_metadata_to_wheels\",\n            default_add_extra_metadata_to_wheels,\n            ctx=ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=version,\n            extra_environ=extra_environ,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n            dist_info_dir=dist_info_dir,\n        )\n        if not isinstance(data_to_add, dict):\n            logger.warning(\n                \"unexpected return type from plugin add_extra_metadata_to_wheels. Duplicate\n    requirements are silently dropped; new ones proceed to source preparation.\n    ``tracks_why`` is ``False`` so graph additions happen before the why-stack\n    is updated.\n\n    Next phase: ``PrepareSource`` (new requirement) or ``[]`` (already seen).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    phase: typing.ClassVar[BootstrapPhase] = BootstrapPhase.START\n    tracks_why: typing.ClassVar[bool] = False\n\n    def run(self, bt: Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"START phase: add to graph, check if already seen.\n\n        _track_why is a no-op for this phase (tracks_why is False),\n        matching the original behavior where graph addition and\n        seen-check happen before pushing onto the why stack.\n\n        Returns:\n            Empty list if already seen (nothing to do).\n            [PrepareSource] if this is new work.\n        \"\"\"\n        wi = self.work_item\n        assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n        assert wi.source_url is not None\n\n        # Overrides\n===================\n\nFromager has two plugin systems that serve different purposes:\n**per-package overrides** replace default behavior for a specific\npackage, while **global hooks** broadcast notifications after events\nfor every package.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n   :doc:`/reference/hooks` documents each override hook's arguments and\n   return values.  :doc:`/customization` covers global hooks with code\n   examples.\n\nComparison\n----------\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 20 40 40\n\n   * - Aspect\n     - Per-Package Overrides\n     - Global Hooks\n   * - **Scope**\n     - One named package\n     - Every package\n   * - **Cardinality**\n     - At most one override module per package\n     - Multiple plugins per hook\n   * - **Semantics**\n     - Replaces the default implementation\n     - Runs in addition to the default\n   * - **Return value**\n     - Used by the caller\n     - None (fire-and-forget)\n   * - **Typical use**\n     - Custom download, build, or resolution logic\n     - Publishing wheels, validation, logging\n\nPer-Package Overrides\n---------------------\n\nAn override module provides alternative implementations for specific\nbuild steps.  Fromager looks up the module by the canonicalized package\nname.  If the module defines the requested method, it is called instead\nof the default; otherwise the default runs.\n\nOverride hooks cover resolution, source acquisition, building,\ndependency extraction, and build environment customization.  Third-party\npackages register overrides via the ``fromager.project_overrides``\nentry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a package name to\na Python module.\n\nSee :doc:`/reference/hooks` for the complete list of hooks and their\narguments.\n\nGlobal Hooks\n------------\n\nGlobal hooks are event callbacks that fire for every package.  All\nregistered plugins for a hook are called sequentially.  They cannot\nalter the build result — they are purely side-effecting notifications.\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Hook\n     - When it fires\n   * - ``post_build``\n     - After a wheel is built from source (not for prebuilt wheels)\n   * - ``prebuilt_wheel``\n     - After a prebuilt wheel is downloaded (not built from source)\n   * - ``post_bootstrap``\n     - After a package is bootstrapped, before its install dependencies\n       are processed\n\nThird-party packages register hooks via the ``fromager.hooks``\nentry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a hook name to\na callable.\n\nSee :doc:`/customization` for examples and argument details.\nPackage Settings\n================\n\nFromager uses a layered settings system to configure how each package\nis resolved, downloaded, patched, and built.  Settings flow from YAML\nfiles on disk through a merge pipeline into a single facade object\nused by the build pipeline.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`/reference/config-reference` documents every configuration\n   field.  :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n\nSettings Loading Flow\n---------------------\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   CLI flags\n   (--settings-file, --settings-dir, --patches-dir)\n         │\n         ▼\n   Settings.from_files()\n   ├── Load settings.yaml ──► SettingsFile (global config)\n   └── Glob settings/*.yaml ──► PackageSettings (one per package)\n         │\n         ▼\n   Settings object (held by WorkContext)\n         │\n         │  package_build_info(\"torch\")  (on demand, cached)\n         ▼\n   PackageBuildInfo\n   (single facade used by the build pipeline)\n\n``PackageBuildInfo`` objects are created lazily the first time a\npackage is queried and cached for the rest of the run.\n\nDirectory Structure\n-------------------\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   overrides/\n   ├── settings.yaml              # Global settings\n   ├── settings/                  # Per-package settings\n   │   ├── torch.yaml\n   │   ├── flash-attn.yaml\n   │   └── ...\n   └── patches/                   # Patches\n       ├── torch/                 # Unversioned (all versions)\n       │   ├── 001-fix.patch\n       │   └── cpu/               # Variant-specific\n       │       └── 002-cpu.patch\n       └── torch-2.4.0/           # Version-specific\n           └── 001-ver.patch\n\nPackage YAML filenames use the canonicalized package name (lowercase,\nhyphens).  All three directories are configurable via CLI flags.\n\nMerge Order\n-----------\n\nSettings are merged from least-specific to most-specific.  Later\nlayers override earlier ones:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   │  1. Pydantic field defaults                      │\n   │     (empty env, default build options, etc.)     │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  2. Global settings.yaml                         │\n   │     (SBOM config, global changelog)              │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  3. Per-package YAML file                        │\n   │     (env, resolver, build options, patches, ...) │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  4. Variant overrides (within package YAML)      │\n   │     (env vars, pre_built, wheel_server_url)      │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  5. Version-specific patches and changelog       │\n   │     (patches/<pkg>-<version>/, changelog entries)│\n   │                                                  │\n   │  6. Override plugin hooks (runtime)              │\n   │     (update_extra_environ can mutate env vars)   │\n   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\nFor environment variables specifically, the merge order within a\nsingle ``get_extra_environ()`` call is: parallel-jobs settings, build\nenvironment paths, package-level ``env``, then variant-level ``env``.\nEntries can reference earlier values using ``$VAR`` template syntax.\n\nPackageBuildInfo Facade\n-----------------------\n\n``PackageBuildInfo`` is the single interface the build pipeline uses to\nquery all package configuration.  It wraps a ``PackageSettings`` and\nadds variant awareness, patch discovery, and template resolution.\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Category\n     - What it provides\n   * - **Identity**\n     - Package name, variant, whether a config file exists, override\n       plugin module\n   * - **Resolution**\n     - Sdist server URL, include wheels/sdists flags, platform\n       filtering, per-package cooldown override\n   * - **Build config**\n     - Environment variables, parallel jobs, exclusive build flag,\n       PEP 517 config settings, build directory\n   * - **Source**\n     - Download URL and filename templates with ``${version}``\n       substitution, git submodule options\n   * - **Patches**\n     - Merged list of unversioned + version-specific + variant-specific\n       patch files, sorted by filename\n   * - **Metadata**\n     - Build tag (from changelog length), annotations, PURL config,\n       pyproject.toml overrides\n\nSee :doc:`/reference/config-reference` for the full field reference.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import logging
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start, _re_resolve_url
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}


def _make_build_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",
    phase: BootstrapPhase = BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version),
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)


class TestPhaseClassVariables:
    """Verify class-variable declarations on each Phase subclass."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "cls, expected_phase, expected_tracks_why",
        [
            (Resolve, BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE, False),
            (Start, BootstrapPhase.START, False),
            (PrepareSource, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE, True),
            (PrepareBuild, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD, True),
            (Build, BootstrapPhase.BUILD, True),
            (ProcessInstallDeps, BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS, True),
            (Complete, BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE, True),
        ],
    )

class Cart:
    def __init__(self, tax_rate=0.0):
        self.items = []
        self.tax_rate = tax_rate

    def add(self, price, qty=1):

    def total(self):
        return compute_total(self.items, self.tax_rate)

def compute_total(items, tax_rate=0.0):
    """Return the total price of items with tax applied.

    items: iterable of (unit_price, quantity)
    """
    subtotal = sum(price * qty for price, qty in items)
    return round(subtotal * (1 + tax_rate), 2)

import math
from collections.abc import Iterable


def distance(a: tuple[float, float], b: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
    return math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])


def perimeter(points: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> float:
    if len(points) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return sum(distance(points[i], points[(i + 1) % len(points)]) for i in range(len(points)))


def centroid(points: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    if not points:
        return None
    n = len(points)
    return (sum(p[0] for p in points) / n, sum(p[1] for p in points) / n)


class Polygon:
    def __init__(
        self,
        points: Iterable[tuple[float, float]],
        name: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.points = list(points)
        self.name = name

    def area(self) -> float:
        s = 0.0
        for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(self.points):
            x2, y2 = self.points[(i + 1) % len(self.points)]
            s += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
        return abs(s) / 2

    def scaled(self, factor: float) -> "Polygon":
        return Polygon([(x * factor, y * factor) for x, y in self.points], self.name)

    def describe(self) -> dict[str, str | int | None | float]:
        return {"name": self.name, "sides": len(self.points), "area": self.area()}

"""A small least-recently-used cache with optional time-based expiry."""

import time
from collections import OrderedDict


class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity, ttl=None, clock=time.monotonic):
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be greater than zero")
        if ttl is not None and ttl < 0:
            raise ValueError("ttl must not be negative")

        self.capacity = capacity
        self.ttl = ttl
        self._clock = clock
        self._items = OrderedDict()
        self._stats = {"hits": 0, "misses": 0, "evictions": 0, "expirations": 0}

    def _is_expired(self, expires_at, now):
        return expires_at is not None and now >= expires_at

    def _remove_expired(self, key, now):
        entry = self._items.get(key)
        if entry is not None and self._is_expired(entry[1], now):
            del self._items[key]
            self._stats["expirations"] += 1
            return True
        return False

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        now = self._clock()
        if self._remove_expired(key, now):
            self._stats["misses"] += 1
            return default

        try:
            value, expires_at = self._items.pop(key)
        except KeyError:
            self._stats["misses"] += 1
            return default

        self._items[key] = (value, expires_at)
        self._stats["hits"] += 1
        return value

    def put(self, key, value):
        now = self._clock()
        self._remove_expired(key, now)
        if key in self._items:
            del self._items[key]
        expires_at = None if self.ttl is None else now + self.ttl
        self._items[key] = (value, expires_at)
        if len(self._items) > self.capacity:
            self._items.popitem(last=False)
            self._stats["evictions"] += 1

    def delete(self, key):
        try:
            del self._items[key]
        except KeyError:
            return False
        return True

    def stats(self):
        return self._stats.copy()

    def __len__(self):
        now = self._clock()
        expired = [key for key, (_, deadline) in self._items.items()
                   if self._is_expired(deadline, now)]
        for key in expired:
            del self._items[key]
            self._stats["expirations"] += 1
        return len(self._items)

    def __contains__(self, key):
        now = self._clock()
        if self._remove_expired(key, now):
            return False
        return key in self._items

diff --git a/tests/test_lru.py b/tests/test_lru.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..24f445d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_lru.py
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+import pytest
+
+from cachelib import LRUCache
+
+
+class FakeClock:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.now = 0.0
+
+    def __call__(self):
+        return self.now
+
+
+def test_lru_eviction_and_get_updates_recency():
+    cache = LRUCache(2)
+    cache.put("a", 1)
+    cache.put("b", 2)
+    assert cache.get("a") == 1
+    cache.put("c", 3)
+
+    assert "a" in cache
+    assert "b" not in cache
+    assert cache.get("b", "missing") == "missing"
+    assert cache.stats() == {"hits": 1, "misses": 1, "evictions": 1, "expirations": 0}
+
+
+def test_update_moves_entry_and_replaces_value():
+    cache = LRUCache(2)
+    cache.put("a", 1)
+    cache.put("b", 2)
+    cache.put("a", 3)
+    cache.put("c", 4)
+
+    assert cache.get("a") == 3
+    assert "b" not in cache
+
+
+def test_ttl_expiration_and_stats():
+    clock = FakeClock()
+    cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=3, clock=clock)
+    cache.put("a", 1)
+    clock.now = 3
+
+    assert cache.get("a", None) is None
+    assert len(cache) == 0
+    assert cache.stats() == {"hits": 0, "misses": 1, "evictions": 0, "expirations": 1}
+
+

import pytest

from cachelib import LRUCache


class FakeClock:
    def __init__(self):
        self.now = 0.0

    def __call__(self):
        return self.now


def test_lru_eviction_and_get_updates_recency():
    cache = LRUCache(2)
    cache.put("a", 1)
    cache.put("b", 2)
    assert cache.get("a") == 1
    cache.put("c", 3)

    assert "a" in cache
    assert "b" not in cache
    assert cache.get("b", "missing") == "missing"
    assert cache.stats() == {"hits": 1, "misses": 1, "evictions": 1, "expirations": 0}


def test_update_moves_entry_and_replaces_value():
    cache = LRUCache(2)
    cache.put("a", 1)
    cache.put("b", 2)
    cache.put("a", 3)
    cache.put("c", 4)

    assert cache.get("a") == 3
    assert "b" not in cache


def test_ttl_expiration_and_stats():
    clock = FakeClock()
    cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=3, clock=clock)
    cache.put("a", 1)
    clock.now = 3

    assert cache.get("a", None) is None
    assert len(cache) == 0
    assert cache.stats() == {"hits": 0, "misses": 1, "evictions": 0, "expirations": 1}


def test_contains_does_not_change_recency_or_hit_stats():
    cache = LRUCache(2)
    cache.put("a", 1)
    cache.put("b", 2)

    assert "a" in cache
    cache.put("c", 3)

    assert "a" not in cache
    assert cache.stats() == {"hits": 0, "misses": 0, "evictions": 1, "expirations": 0}


def test_delete_reports_presence_including_none_values():
    cache = LRUCache(1)
    cache.put("a", None)

    assert cache.delete("a") is True
    assert cache.delete("a") is False


@pytest.mark.parametrize("capacity", [0, -1])
def test_nonpositive_capacity_is_rejected(capacity):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        LRUCache(capacity)

import argparse
import json
import sys


def count(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()
    return {"lines": text.count("\n"), "words": len(text.split()), "chars": len(text)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wc")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    total = {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0}
    files = []
    rc = 0
    for path in args.files:
        try:
            c = count(path)
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"wc: {path}: {e.strerror}", file=sys.stderr)
            rc = 1
            continue
        if args.json:
            files.append({"path": path, **c})
        else:
            print(f"{c['lines']:>8}{c['words']:>8}{c['chars']:>8} {path}")
        for k in total:
            total[k] += c[k]
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"files": files, "total": total}))
    elif len(args.files) > 1:
        print(f"{total['lines']:>8}{total['words']:>8}{total['chars']:>8} total")
    return rc

import json

from wc.cli import main


def test_text(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    assert main([str(p)]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == f"       2       3      16 {p}\n"


def test_json_counts_files_and_total(tmp_path, capsys):
    first = tmp_path / "a.txt"
    second = tmp_path / "b.txt"
    first.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    second.write_text("one two")

    assert main(["--json", str(first), str(second)]) == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert json.loads(captured.out) == {
        "files": [
            {"path": str(first), "lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16},
            {"path": str(second), "lines": 0, "words": 2, "chars": 7},
        ],
        "total": {"lines": 2, "words": 5, "chars": 23},
    }
    assert captured.err == ""


def test_json_missing_file_reports_error_and_omits_missing(tmp_path, capsys):
    existing = tmp_path / "a.txt"
    existing.write_text("hello\n")
    missing = tmp_path / "missing.txt"

    assert main(["--json", str(existing), str(missing)]) == 1
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert json.loads(captured.out) == {
        "files": [{"path": str(existing), "lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6}],
        "total": {"lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6},
    }
    assert captured.err == f"wc: {missing}: No such file or directory\n"

"""Parsing and aggregation for the access log format."""

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import math
import re
from typing import Iterable


@dataclass
class Record:
    ts: datetime
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    latency_ms: float
    bytes: int


@dataclass
class Summary:
    total: int
    malformed: int
    by_status: dict[int, int]
    by_method: dict[str, int]
    p50_latency_ms: float
    p95_latency_ms: float
    bytes_total: int
    error_rate: float
    top_paths: list[tuple[str, int]]


_LINE = re.compile(
    r"(?P<timestamp>\S+) (?P<method>\S+) (?P<path>\S+) "
    r"(?P<status>\d+) (?P<latency>\S+)(?: (?P<bytes>\S+))?"
)


def parse_line(line: str) -> Record | None:
    """Parse one access log line, returning None when it is malformed."""
    match = _LINE.fullmatch(line.strip())
    if match is None:
        return None

    try:
        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(match.group("timestamp").replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if ts.tzinfo is None or ts.utcoffset() is None:
            return None
        ts = ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)
        status = int(match.group("status"))
        latency_ms = float(match.group("latency"))
        byte_count = int(match.group("bytes") or 0)
        if not math.isfinite(latency_ms) or latency_ms < 0 or byte_count < 0:
            return None
    except (ValueError, OverflowError):
        return None

    return Record(
        ts=ts,
        method=match.group("method"),
        path=match.group("path"),
        status=status,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        bytes=byte_count,
    )


def summarize(lines: Iterable[str]) -> Summary:
    """Summarize parsed records while counting skipped malformed lines."""
    records: list[Record] = []
    malformed = 0
    for line in lines:
        record = parse_line(line)
        if record is None:
            malformed += 1
        else:
            records.append(record)

    latencies = sorted(record.latency_ms for record in records)

    def percentile(fraction: float) -> float:
        if not latencies:
            return 0.0
        rank = math.ceil(fraction * len(latencies))
        return latencies[rank - 1]

    paths = Counter(record.path for record in records)
    total = len(records)
    return Summary(
        total=total,
        malformed=malformed,
        by_status=dict(Counter(record.status for record in records)),
        by_method=dict(Counter(record.method for record in records)),
        p50_latency_ms=percentile(0.50),
        p95_latency_ms=percentile(0.95),
        bytes_total=sum(record.bytes for record in records),
        error_rate=(sum(record.status >= 500 for record in records) / total if total else 0.0),
        top_paths=sorted(paths.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:5],
    )

The canonical docs cover the full reference; this skill adds decision-making, failure-mode prevention, and ready-to-extend patterns on top.\n\n## Pick the language\n\nDecide before writing any code. Order:\n\n1. **The user named it.** `@cursor/sdk`, `cursor-sdk`, `cursor_sdk`, `npm install`, `pip install`, `import { Agent } from \"@cursor/sdk\"`, `from cursor_sdk import` - go with what they named.\n2. **The codebase signals it.** `pyproject.toml` / `requirements.txt` / `uv.lock` / `.py` files → Python. `package.json` / `tsconfig.json` / `.ts` files → TypeScript. If the integration will live in a polyglot repo, ask which subdirectory it goes into.\n3. **No signal either way.** Ask one short question and wait: *\"TypeScript or Python?\"* Don't pick for them.\n\nThe rest of this skill shows TypeScript and Python side by side. Concepts are identical; syntax differs - camelCase vs snake_case, async-by-default vs sync-default-with-async-mirror, `await using` vs `with`.\n\n## Voice and Posture\n\nThis skill helps the user **build** with the SDK. It is not the place to validate, congratulate, or sell the SDK as a choice. The user's intent is the input; your job is execution.\n\n- **When the user names the SDK explicitly** (says \"Codex SDK\", `@cursor/sdk`, `cursor-sdk`, `Agent.create`, `Agent.prompt`, etc.): assume they know what the SDK is and have decided to use it. No \"good news\", no \"the SDK is perfect for this\", no \"this is almost exactly the pattern X is designed for\".\n- **When the user describes a problem the SDK fits but doesn't name it** (\"I want a bot that reviews my PRs\", \"I want a script that asks Codex questions about my repo\"): the SDK isn't yet a confirmed choice. If they push back or want options, give options.\n- **In either case, don't restate the user's intent back to them.** They know what they want. Get to the design.\n\nAvoid these specific openers (and their close cousins):\n\n- \"Good news: this is exactly the pattern...\"\n- \"The SDK is built for this shape.\"\n- \"Great, you've come to the right place.\"\n- \"This is almost exactly the X the SDK is designed for.\"\n- Any lede that compliments the user's choice or restates their goal in flattering terms.\n\nPrefer:\n\n- Open with the design decision or the first thing they need to know.\n- If you genuinely have a design choice to flag (local vs cloud, prompt vs send, sync vs stream, sync Python vs async Python), name it in one sentence and explain why.\n\n## The Three Invocation Patterns\n\nAlmost every SDK integration collapses to one of these three shapes. Pick the one that fits the job, don't mix them.\n\n### 1. `Agent.prompt(...)` - one-shot\n\nUse for fire-and-forget scripts, GitHub Actions steps, or any \"send this prompt, get a result, exit\" flow. No streaming, no follow-ups, no cleanup to remember. If you're reaching for this and then immediately resuming, you wanted pattern 2 instead.\n\n**TypeScript:**\n\n```typescript\nimport { Agent } from \"@cursor/sdk\";\n\nconst result = await Agent.prompt(\"Refactor src/utils.ts for readability\", {\n  apiKey: process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY!,\n  model: { id: \"composer-2.5\" },\n  local: { cwd: process.cwd() },\n});\nconsole.log(result.status, result.result);\n```\n\n**Python:**\n\n```python\nimport os\nfrom cursor_sdk import Agent, AgentOptions, LocalAgentOptions\n\nresult = Agent.prompt(\n    \"Refactor src/utils.py for readability\",\n    AgentOptions(\n        api_key=os.environ[\"CURSOR_API_KEY\"],\n        model=\"composer-2.5\",\n        local=LocalAgentOptions(cwd=os.getcwd()),\n    ),\n)\nprint(result.status, result.result)\n```\n\n### 2. `Agent.create(...)` + `agent.send(...)` - durable with follow-ups\n\nUse when you need streaming, multi-turn conversation, or lifecycle operations (cancel, status listener). This is the shape of most non-trivial integrations.\n\n**TypeScript:**\n\n```typescript\nimport { Agent } from \"@cursor/sdk\";\n\nawait using agent = await Agent.create({\n  apiKey: process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY!,\n  model: { id: \"composer-2.5\" },\n  local: { cwd: process.cwd() },\n});\n\nconst run = await agent.send(\"Find the bug in src/auth.ts\");\nfor await (const event of run.stream()) {\n  if (event.type === \"assistant\") {\n    for (const block of event.message.content) {\n      if (block.type === \"text\") process.stdout.write(block.text);\n    }\n  }\n}\nawait run.wait();\n\n// Follow-up keeps full conversation context.\nconst run2 = await agent.send(\"Now write a regression test for it\");\nawait run2.wait();\n```\n\n**Python:**\n\n```python\nimport os\nfrom cursor_sdk import Agent, LocalAgentOptions\n\nwith Agent.create(\n    model=\"composer-2.5\",\n    api_key=os.environ[\"CURSOR_API_KEY\"],\n    local=LocalAgentOptions(cwd=os.getcwd()),\n) as agent:\n    run = agent.send(\"Find the bug in src/auth.py\")\n    for message in run.messages():\n        if message.type == \"assistant\":\n            for block in message.message.content:\n                if block.type == \"text\":\n                    print(block.text, end=\"\")\n    run.wait()\n\n    # Follow-up keeps full conversation context.\n    run2 = agent.send(\"Now write a regression test for it\")\n    run2.wait()\n```\n\nThe Python SDK is sync by default. For servers, bots, and concurrent orchestration, use `AsyncClient.launch_bridge(...)` as an async context manager and `AsyncAgent`. There's no global async default client - instantiate one per event loop, and never mix sync and async clients in the same code path.\n\n### 3. `Agent.resume(...)` - pick up an existing agent later\n\nUse across process boundaries: a cron that continues last night's cleanup, a webhook that extends a user's agent, an interactive CLI that reloads conversation state. Runtime is auto-detected from the ID prefix - `bc-` is cloud, anything else is local.\n\n**TypeScript:**\n\n```typescript\nawait using agent = await Agent.resume(previousAgentId, {\n  apiKey: process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY!,\n});\nconst run = await agent.send(\"Also update the changelog\");\nawait run.wait();\n```\n\n**Python:**\n\n```python\nimport os\nfrom cursor_sdk import Agent, AgentOptions\n\nwith Agent.resume(\n    previous_agent_id,\n    AgentOptions(api_key=os.environ[\"CURSOR_API_KEY\"]),\n) as agent:\n    run = agent.send(\"Also update the changelog\")\n    run.wait()\n```\n\n**Inline MCP servers are not persisted across resume** - they often carry secrets and live in memory only. Pass them again on the resume call in either language.\n\n## Top Five Traps\n\nThese trip up almost every new integration. They're all easy to prevent once you know about them.\n\n### 1. Picking the wrong runtime by accident\n\n`AgentOptions` doesn't require `local` or `cloud`; the SDK selects local when neither is set. The trap: if you intended a cloud agent and forgot the `cloud` field, you get a local agent silently - no error, just a local agent ID and a local executor.\n\n- **TypeScript:** pass `cloud: { repos: [...] }` for cloud, `local: { cwd }` for local - even though local is the default.\n- **Python:** pass `cloud=CloudAgentOptions(repos=[...])` or `local=LocalAgentOptions(cwd=...)`.\n\nAlways set one of the two explicitly. The cost is one line; the cost of not noticing for an hour is much more.\n\n### 2. Two kinds of failure, one instinct to conflate them\n\nA thrown `CursorAgentError` means the run **never executed** (auth, config, network). A returned `result.status == \"error\"` means the run **did execute and failed**. Different fixes, different exit codes, different observability.\n\n**TypeScript:**\n\n```typescript\nimport { Agent, CursorAgentError } from \"@cursor/sdk\";\n\ntry {\n  const run = await agent.send(prompt);\n  const result = await run.wait();\n  if (result.status === \"error\") {\n    // Run started but failed mid-flight. Inspect transcript, git state, tool outputs.\n    console.error(\"run failed: \" + result.id);\n    process.exit(2);\n  }\n} catch (err) {\n  if (err instanceof CursorAgentError) {\n    // Didn't start. Auth, config, network. Fix environment, retry.\n    console.error(\"startup failed: \" + err.message + \", retryable=\" + err.isRetryable);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  throw err;\n}\n```\n\n**Python:**\n\n```python\nimport sys\nfrom cursor_sdk import CursorAgentError\n\ntry:\n    run = agent.send(prompt)\n    result = run.wait()\n    if result.status == \"error\":\n        # Run started but failed mid-flight. Inspect transcript, git state, tool outputs.\n        print(\"run failed: \" + result.id, file=sys.stderr)\n        sys.exit(2)\nexcept CursorAgentError as err:\n    # Didn't start. Auth, config, network. Fix environment, retry.\n    print(\n        \"startup failed: \" + err.message + \", retryable=\" + str(err.is_retryable),\n        file=sys.stderr,\n    )\n    sys.exit(1)\n```\n\n### 3. Forgetting to dispose leaks resources\n\nThe SDK holds handles to local executors, persisted run stores, and HTTP clients. Skipping disposal leaks child processes, open databases, and (in long-running services) memory.\n\n- **TypeScript:** `await using agent = await Agent.create(...)` is the cleanest path. Otherwise wrap in `try/finally` with `await agent[Symbol.asyncDispose]()`. `Agent.prompt(...)` disposes for you.\n- **Python (sync):** `with Agent.create(...) as agent:` is the cleanest path. Otherwise call `agent.close()` in a `finally`. Long-running processes that rely on the module-level default client should call `close_default_client()` at shutdown.\n- **Python (async):** nest two async context managers - `async with await AsyncClient.launch_bridge(...) as client:` then `async with await client.agents.create(...) as agent:`. `Agent.prompt(...)` disposes for you.\n\n### 4. Streaming is optional but `wait()` is almost always required\n\nThe stream is how you observe; `wait()` is how you get the terminal result. You can skip streaming, but skipping `wait()` means you can't tell whether the run finished, errored, or was cancelled, and you'll leak the run's internal watchers. Always call `wait()`. If you don't want live output, call `wait()` alone.\n\n- **TypeScript:** `run.stream()` is an async iterable of `SDKMessage`. `await run.wait()` returns `RunResult`.\n- **Python:** `run.messages()` yields typed SDK messages; `run.events()` yields lower-level envelopes. `run.wait()` returns `RunResult`. Async equivalents are `async for ...` and `await run.wait()`. Convenience helpers: `run.text()` blocks on `wait()` and returns the final assistant text; `run.iter_text()` streams text-only chunks. `run.stream()` is an alias for `run.messages()`.\n\n### 5. Not every `run` operation is supported on every runtime\n\n`Run` exposes a handful of operations - stream/messages, wait, cancel, conversation - and detached or rehydrated runs (handles you got from `Agent.getRun(...)` after the live event store closed) may not support all of them. Guard with `supports(...)`:\n\n```typescript\nif (run.supports(\"cancel\")) await run.cancel();\nif (run.supports(\"conversation\")) console.log(await run.conversation());\n```\n\n```python\nif run.supports(\"cancel\"):\n    run.cancel()\nif run.supports(\"conversation\"):\n    print(run.conversation())\n```\n\n`run.unsupportedReason(op)` (TypeScript) / `run.unsupported_reason(op)` (Python) tells you why.\n\n## Local vs Cloud, in one sentence each\n\n- **Local** - runs on the caller's machine against `cwd`, reuses their environment and credentials. Good for dev loops and CI that already has a repo checkout.\n- **Cloud** - runs on a Codex-hosted VM against a freshly cloned repo. Good for long jobs, fire-and-forget automation, and opening real PRs (`autoCreatePR: true` in TypeScript; `auto_create_pr=True` in Python).\n\n## Auth, minimum viable\n\n```bash\nexport CURSOR_API_KEY=\"cursor_...\"  # user API key or team service-account key\n```\n\nBoth SDKs read `CURSOR_API_KEY` when no key is passed explicitly. User keys live at [Codex Dashboard → Integrations](https://cursor.com/dashboard/integrations); team service-account keys live in Team Settings → Service accounts. Team Admin API keys are not yet supported.\n\nIf you're seeing 401s, the usual suspects are: key pasted with surrounding whitespace, key minted against a different environment, or the key belongs to a user without repo access for a cloud run.\n\n## Model Selection\n\nDon't hardcode unusual model IDs without confirming the caller has access - model lists evolve.\n\n**TypeScript:**\n\n```typescript\nimport { Codex } from \"@cursor/sdk\";\n\nconst models = await Codex.models.list({ apiKey: process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY! });\n```\n\n**Python:**\n\n```python\nfrom cursor_sdk import Codex\n\nmodels = Codex.models.list()  # falls back to CURSOR_API_KEY\n```\n\n`composer-2.5` is the current default for most integrations. `{ id: \"auto\" }` (TS) / `model=\"auto\"` (Python) lets the server pick. `Codex.models.list()` returns valid IDs, per-model parameter definitions (reasoning effort, max mode), and preset variants for the calling account.\n\nModel is **required for local** in both SDKs. For cloud, TypeScript falls back to a server-resolved default when omitted; Python documents it as required across both runtimes. Pass one regardless to keep behavior predictable.\n\n## MCP Servers\n\nBoth SDKs use the same conceptual model: HTTP transport (with static `headers` or OAuth `auth`) or stdio (with `command` / `args` / `env`). Pass servers inline on `Agent.create` or `agent.send` for the most common case.\n\n- **Local agents** can use stdio or HTTP servers available on the caller's machine. If a local MCP server requires OAuth login, the SDK can reuse a saved login from the Codex app but can't open a browser to sign you in.\n- **Cloud agents** support both HTTP and stdio (stdio runs inside the cloud VM). HTTP `headers` and `auth` are handled by Codex's backend and redacted before the VM sees them. Stdio `env` values are passed into the VM - treat them like any runtime secret.\n- **Inline servers fully replace creation-time servers on a per-send override - not merged.**\n- **If you resume an agent and still need MCP tools, pass servers again on the resume call.** Inline servers are not persisted.\n\nFor full schema and authentication options, see the SDK docs for each language and [Codex MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp).\n\n## Production Best Practices\n\nApply these to any integration that runs unattended:\n\n1. **Always dispose.** `await using` (TypeScript) or `with ... as agent:` (Python) is the cleanest path. Non-negotiable.\n2. **Distinguish startup failures from run failures.** Exit code 1 for thrown `CursorAgentError`, exit code 2 for `result.status == \"error\"`, exit code 0 only for `finished`.\n3. **Log `run.id` and `agent.agentId` / `agent.agent_id` immediately after `send()`** before streaming. If the stream hangs, the IDs are what you need to investigate in the dashboard or via `Agent.getRun(...)` / `Agent.get_run(...)`.\n4. **Respect `error.isRetryable` / `err.is_retryable`.** It's the backend telling you the specific failure is safe to retry. Python errors also expose `retry_after` (HTTP-style seconds value or date) - honor it before falling back to exponential backoff. Blind retries can cause duplicate cloud runs.\n5. **Don't load ambient settings unless you mean to.** The default in TypeScript is `local.settingSources: []`; the default in Python is no `local.setting_sources`. Both mean \"inline config only\". Opting into `\"all\"` loads project/user/team/MDM settings from the caller's environment, which is rarely what you want from a service. Setting sources have no effect on cloud agents - cloud always honors team/project/plugins.\n6. **For cloud agents in CI, set `skipReviewerRequest: true` (TypeScript) / `skip_reviewer_request=True` (Python)** unless a human should be paged - it suppresses the reviewer-request step and keeps PR notifications quiet.\n7. **Always pass `apiKey` / `api_key` explicitly** in shared-infrastructure code instead of relying on the env var. Makes the credential dependency obvious and prevents cross-tenant mistakes.\n8. **Prefer the one-shot `Agent.prompt(...)` for true one-shots** - it disposes for you and is harder to leak.\n\n## Observing a Run You Didn't Launch\n\nYou can inspect any agent or run by ID later. Cloud IDs that start with `bc-` auto-route to the cloud API; anything else is local.\n\n**TypeScript:**\n\n```typescript\nconst info = await Agent.get(\"bc-abc123\", { apiKey });\nconst run = await Agent.getRun(runId, { runtime: \"cloud\", agentId: \"bc-abc123\", apiKey });\n\n// Local: you need the cwd where the agent was created.\nconst localList = await Agent.list({ runtime: \"local\", cwd: process.cwd() });\n```\n\n**Python:**\n\n```python\nfrom cursor_sdk import CursorClient\n\nwith CursorClient.launch_bridge(workspace=\".\") as client:\n    info = client.agents.get(\"bc-abc123\")\n    run = client.agents.get_run(run_id)\n\n    # Local: filter by cwd.\n    local_list = client.agents.list(runtime=\"local\", cwd=\".\")\n```\n\nA cloud `bc-`-prefixed agent ID is **not** a run ID. If you only have a run ID (from a log or a webhook), pass it to `getRun` / `get_run` with the runtime hint; don't confuse the two.\n\n## Offering a Canvas\n\nIf the user's integration monitors, lists, or visualizes agents - dashboards of active runs, conversation replays, tool-call timelines - offer a Codex Canvas to render it. If they accept, defer entirely to the `canvas` skill.\n\n## What This Skill Doesn't Cover\n\n- The [Cloud Agents REST API](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints) (`/v1/agents/*`). Use it from languages without a first-party SDK, or when you want a minimal HTTP surface.\n- `.cursor/hooks.json` hooks. Both SDKs respect them; neither manages them. See [Hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks).\n- Self-hosted cloud (private workers, self-hosted pools, my-machines). See [Self-hosted pool](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted-pool) and related docs.\n- SDKs in languages other than TypeScript and Python. The REST API is the portable option there.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
